   152→    @property

   154→        gf = super().global_features
   155→        if "spectra_fingerprint" in self.extra_features:

   159→    def forward(
   160→        self,
   161→        nodes: torch.Tensor,
   162→        edges: torch.Tensor,
   163→        mask: torch.Tensor,
   164→        t: torch.Tensor,
   165→        num_peaks: torch.Tensor = None,

   168→        ion_vec: torch.Tensor = None,
   169→        form_vec: torch.Tensor = None,
   170→        intens: torch.Tensor = None,
   171→    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
   172→        """
   173→        Run the forward pass for Spec2MolMetaArch.
   174→        This provides explicit arguments for spectral features while leveraging
   175→        DigressMetaArch's noise logic.
   176→        """
   177→        return super().forward(
   178→            nodes=nodes,
   179→            edges=edges,
   180→            mask=mask,
   181→            t=t,
   182→            num_peaks=num_peaks,
   183→            types=types,
   184→            instruments=instruments,
   185→            ion_vec=ion_vec,
   186→            form_vec=form_vec,
   187→            intens=intens,
   188→        )
   189→
   190→    def forward_backward(
   191→        self,
   192→        nodes: torch.Tensor,
   193→        edges: torch.Tensor,
   194→        mask: torch.Tensor,
   195→        num_peaks: torch.Tensor = None,
   196→        types: torch.Tensor = None,
   197→        instruments: torch.Tensor = None,
   198→        ion_vec: torch.Tensor = None,
   199→        form_vec: torch.Tensor = None,
   200→        intens: torch.Tensor = None,
   201→    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
   202→        """
   203→        Noise the input batch, predict the clean graph, compute loss and backpropagate.
   204→
   205→        Wraps DigressMetaArch.forward_backward with explicit spectral arguments
   206→        that are forwarded to compute_extra_features for spectra fingerprinting.
   207→
   208→        Args:
   209→            nodes: Node features of shape (bs, n, natoms).
   210→            edges: Edge features of shape (bs, n, n, nedges).
   211→            mask: Mask tensor of shape (bs, n).
   212→            num_peaks: Number of peaks per spectrum.
   213→            types: Peak type tensors.
   214→            instruments: Instrument identifiers.
   215→            ion_vec: Ion vector representation.
   216→            form_vec: Formula vector representation.
   217→            intens: Peak intensity tensors.
   218→
   219→        Returns:
   220→            tuple: (pN, pE, loss) — predicted node/edge probabilities and scalar loss.
   221→                All may be None on non-last ranks in pipeline parallelism.
   222→        """
   223→        return super().forward_backward(
   224→            nodes=nodes,
   225→            edges=edges,
   226→            mask=mask,
   227→            num_peaks=num_peaks,
   228→            types=types,
   229→            instruments=instruments,
   230→            ion_vec=ion_vec,
   231→            form_vec=form_vec,
   232→            intens=intens,
   233→        )
   234→
   235→    def compute_extra_features(
   236→        self,
   237→        nodes: torch.Tensor,
   238→        edges: torch.Tensor,
   239→        mask: torch.Tensor,
   240→        t: torch.Tensor,
   241→        **kwargs,
   242→    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
   243→        """
   244→        Compute extra node and global features for the current graph state.
   245→
   246→        Delegates standard features (laplacian, node_cycle, valence) to the parent,
   247→        then appends the spectra fingerprint if configured.
   248→        """
   249→        # Temporarily hide spectra_fingerprint so the parent doesn't hit ValueError
   250→        all_features = self.extra_features
   251→        self.extra_features = [
   252→            f for f in all_features if f in DigressMetaArch.known_extra_features
   253→        ]
   254→
   255→        pos_emb, y = super().compute_extra_features(nodes, edges, mask, t)
   256→
   257→        # Restore full feature list
   258→        self.extra_features = all_features
   259→
   260→        if "spectra_fingerprint" in all_features:
   261→            fp = spectra_fingerprint(
   262→                kwargs["num_peaks"],
   263→                kwargs["types"],
   264→                kwargs["instruments"],
   265→                kwargs["ion_vec"],
   266→                kwargs["form_vec"],
   267→                kwargs["intens"],
   268→                self.spectra_encoder,
   269→                self.merge_function,
   270→            )
   271→            y = torch.cat([y, fp], dim=-1)
   272→
   273→        return pos_emb, y

    79→def do_eval(
    80→    model: Spec2MolMetaArch,
    81→    eval_loader: DataLoader,
    82→    device: torch.device,
    83→    expected_bs: int | None = None,
    84→) -> dict[str, float]:
    85→    DisableLog("rdApp.*")
    86→    metrics = defaultdict(list)
    87→    for batch in tqdm(
    88→        eval_loader, desc="evaluation", disable=not dist.is_main_process()
    89→    ):
    90→        # Move the elements to the device of interest
    91→        batch = [v.to(device) if isinstance(v, torch.Tensor) else v for v in batch]
    92→
    93→        # Unpack the 10-element tuple
    94→        (
    95→            nodes,
    96→            edges,
    97→            mask,
    98→            num_peaks,
    99→            types,
   100→            instruments,
   101→            ion_vec,
   102→            form_vec,
   103→            intens,
   104→            smiles,
   105→        ) = batch
   106→
   107→        # If last batch, then size will be < to the one planned by schedule
   108→        # To avoid error -> skip it when there is a schedule (ie pp)
   109→        if model.eval_schedule:
   110→            if nodes.shape[0] != expected_bs:
   111→                continue
   112→
   113→        # Noise the elements
   114→        nodes_noised, edges_noised, sampled_t = model.noiser(nodes, edges, mask)
   115→
   116→        # Compute the predictions
   117→        pN, pE = model.forward(
   118→            nodes_noised,
   119→            edges_noised,
   120→            mask,
   121→            sampled_t,
   122→            num_peaks=num_peaks,
   123→            types=types,
   124→            instruments=instruments,
   125→            ion_vec=ion_vec,
   126→            form_vec=form_vec,
   127→            intens=intens,
   128→        )
   129→
   130→        # Non-last ranks in pipeline parallelism get None outputs;
   131→        # they must keep looping so every rank calls schedule.step().
   132→        if pN is None or pE is None:
   133→            continue
   134→
   135→        # Make the prediction graph
   136→        N_ = torch.nn.functional.one_hot(pN.argmax(-1), num_classes=pN.shape[-1])
   137→        E_ = torch.nn.functional.one_hot(pE.argmax(-1), num_classes=pE.shape[-1])
   138→
   139→        # Convert the graph to smiles
   140→        true_smiles = batch_graph_to_smiles(nodes, edges, mask, model.valid_elements)
   141→        pred_smiles = batch_graph_to_smiles(N_, E_, mask, model.valid_elements)
   142→
   143→        # Compute the metrics
   144→        batch_metrics = compute_metrics(
   145→            pred_smiles,
   146→            true_smiles,
   147→            pN,
   148→            pE,
   149→            nodes,
   150→            edges,
   151→            mask,
   152→        )
   153→
   154→        # Compute accuracy per node type
   155→        target_nodes = nodes.argmax(-1)
   156→        pred_nodes = pN.argmax(-1)
   157→        valid_mask = mask.bool()
   158→
   159→        target_nodes_flat = target_nodes[valid_mask]
   160→        pred_nodes_flat = pred_nodes[valid_mask]
   161→
   162→        for i, atom_type in enumerate(model.valid_elements):
   163→            atom_mask = target_nodes_flat == i
   164→            if atom_mask.sum() > 0:
   165→                acc = (pred_nodes_flat[atom_mask] == i).float().mean().item()
   166→                batch_metrics[f"accuracy_node_{atom_type}"] = [acc]
   167→
   168→        # Compute accuracy per edge type
   169→        target_edges = edges.argmax(-1)
   170→        pred_edges = pE.argmax(-1)
   171→        edge_mask = mask.unsqueeze(2) * mask.unsqueeze(1)
   172→        edge_mask = edge_mask.bool()
   173→
   174→        target_edges_flat = target_edges[edge_mask]
   175→        pred_edges_flat = pred_edges[edge_mask]
   176→
   177→        if len(target_edges_flat) > 0:
   178→            acc_edge = (pred_edges_flat == target_edges_flat).float().mean().item()
   179→            batch_metrics["accuracy_edge_global"] = [acc_edge]
   180→
   181→        for i, edge_type in enumerate(TYPE_EDGES):
   182→            edge_type_mask = target_edges_flat == i
   183→            if edge_type_mask.sum() > 0:
   184→                acc = (pred_edges_flat[edge_type_mask] == i).float().mean().item()
   185→                batch_metrics[f"accuracy_edge_{str(edge_type)}"] = [acc]
   186→
   187→        # Accumulate metrics
   188→        for k, v in batch_metrics.items():
   189→            metrics[k].extend(v)
   190→
   191→    # Average and print metrics
   192→    final_metrics = {}
   193→    for k, v in metrics.items():
   194→        if len(v) > 0:
   195→            final_metrics[k] = sum(v) / len(v)
   196→        else:
   197→            final_metrics[k] = 0.0
   198→
   199→    return final_metrics

   202→def generate_samples(
   203→    model: Spec2MolMetaArch,
   204→    num_samples: int,
   205→    num_nodes_dist: torch.Tensor,
   206→    batch_size: int,
   207→) -> tuple[float, float, list[str]]:
   208→    print(f"Generating {num_samples} graphs in batches of {batch_size}...")
   209→    all_gen_smiles = []
   210→    all_gen_smiles_digress = []
   211→    samples_generated = 0
   212→
   213→    while samples_generated < num_samples:
   214→        n = (
   215→            num_nodes_dist.unsqueeze(0)
   216→            .expand((batch_size, -1))
   217→            .multinomial(1)
   218→            .squeeze(-1)
   219→            + 1
   220→        )
   221→
   222→        try:
   223→            gen_N, gen_E, gen_mask = model.generate(
   224→                num_samples=n, max_nodes=n.max(), progress_bar=True
   225→            )
   226→
   227→            gen_smiles = batch_graph_to_smiles(
   228→                gen_N, gen_E, gen_mask, model.valid_elements
   229→            )
   230→            all_gen_smiles.extend(gen_smiles)
   231→
   232→            gen_smiles_digress = batch_graph_to_smiles_digress(
   233→                gen_N, gen_E, gen_mask, model.valid_elements
   234→            )
   235→            all_gen_smiles_digress.extend(gen_smiles_digress)
   236→
   237→        except LinAlgError:
   238→            print("LinAlgError during generation batch, skipping batch...")
   239→            continue
   240→
   241→        samples_generated += batch_size
   242→
   243→    # Trim to exactly num_samples to avoid overshoot bias in validity metrics.
   244→    all_gen_smiles = all_gen_smiles[:num_samples]
   245→    all_gen_smiles_digress = all_gen_smiles_digress[:num_samples]

   247→    valid_smiles = [s for s in all_gen_smiles if s]
   248→    valid_smiles_digress = [s for s in all_gen_smiles_digress if s]

   251→    validity_digress = (
   252→        len(valid_smiles_digress) / len(all_gen_smiles_digress)
   253→        if all_gen_smiles_digress
   254→        else 0
   255→    )
   256→
   257→    return validity, validity_digress, valid_smiles

1→import torch
     2→from torch import nn
     3→
     4→from annotix_ml.spectraencoder.model.spectra_encoder import SpectraEncoder
     5→
     6→
     7→def spectra_fingerprint(
     8→    num_peaks: torch.Tensor,
     9→    types: torch.Tensor,
    10→    instruments: torch.Tensor,
    11→    ion_vec: torch.Tensor,
    12→    form_vec: torch.Tensor,
    13→    intens: torch.Tensor,
    14→    spectra_encoder: SpectraEncoder,
    15→    projection: nn.Module,
    16→) -> torch.Tensor:
    17→    """
    18→    Compute the fingerprint of a spectra within a batch using a SpectraEncoder.
    19→
    20→    This function mimics the idea of extra feature functions in
    21→    `annotix_ml.graphtransf.math.extra_features`, providing a global feature
    22→    (the fingerprint) for the given spectral data.
    23→
    24→    Args:
    25→        num_peaks (torch.Tensor): Number of peaks for each spectrum (bs).
    26→        types (torch.Tensor): Peak types for each spectrum (bs, max_len).
    27→        instruments (torch.Tensor): Instrument indices for each spectrum (bs).
    28→        ion_vec (torch.Tensor): Ion/adduct indices for each peak (bs, max_len).
    29→        form_vec (torch.Tensor): Formula embeddings for each peak (bs, max_len, formula_dim).
    30→        intens (torch.Tensor): Intensity values for each peak (bs, max_len).
    31→        spectra_encoder (SpectraEncoder): Trained SpectraEncoder model instance.
    32→
    33→    Returns:
    34→        torch.Tensor: Spectra fingerprints of shape (bs, output_size).
    35→    """
    36→    # Remake the batch dictionary expected by SpectraEncoder
    37→    batch = {
    38→        "num_peaks": num_peaks,
    39→        "types": types,
    40→        "instruments": instruments,
    41→        "ion_vec": ion_vec,
    42→        "form_vec": form_vec,
    43→        "intens": intens,
    44→    }
    45→
    46→    # The SpectraEncoder expects the batch dictionary directly
    47→    with torch.no_grad():
    48→        # SpectraEncoder.forward returns (output, aux_outputs)
    49→        enc_output, _ = spectra_encoder(batch)
    50→        fingerprint = projection(enc_output)
    51→
    52→    return fingerprint
    53→

    65→            valid_elements (list[str], optional): List of valid atom symbols. If None, elements
    66→                are automatically extracted from the dataset.
    67→            sanitizer (Callable, optional): A function to further filter molecules based on
    68→                their graph representation.
    69→            cache_path (str, optional): Path to a .pt cache file. If the file exists it is
    70→                loaded directly; otherwise the dataset is built and saved there.
    71→            save_cache (bool): Whether to write the cache file after building. Set to False
    72→                on non-main ranks in distributed training to avoid concurrent writes.
    73→        """
    74→        super().__init__()
    75→        if isinstance(data, (str, PosixPath)):
    76→            data = pd.read_csv(data)
    77→
    78→        elif isinstance(data, DataFrame):
    79→            pass
    80→
    81→        else:
    82→            raise TypeError(
    83→                f"{type(data)} is not accepted to instantiate GraphDataset."
    84→            )
    85→
    86→        if split:
    87→            data = data[data[split_column] == split]
    88→
    89→        # Extract SMILES list
    90→        smiles_list = data[smile_column].to_list()
    91→
    92→        # Try to load from cache if a cache path is provided
    93→        if cache_path is not None and os.path.isfile(cache_path):
    94→            if verbose:
    95→                print(f"Loading dataset from cache: {cache_path}")
    96→            cache = torch.load(cache_path, weights_only=False)
    97→            self.smiles = cache["smiles"]
    98→            self.valid_elements = cache["valid_elements"]
    99→            self.nodes_distribution = cache["nodes_distribution"]
   100→            self.edges_distribution = cache["edges_distribution"]
   101→            self.num_atoms_dist = cache["num_atoms_dist"]
   102→            self.max_weight = cache["max_weight"]
   103→
   104→        else:
   105→            if valid_elements is None:
   106→                # Auto-detect atoms from the dataset
   107→                self.valid_elements = _extract_atoms_from_smiles(smiles_list)
   108→            else:
   109→                self.valid_elements = valid_elements
   110→
   111→            smiles, nodes, edges = self._build(smiles_list, sanitizer, verbose)
   112→
   113→            self.smiles = smiles
   114→
   115→            # Compute the distribution of nodes
   116→            node_number = torch.cat(nodes).sum(0)  # (natoms)
   117→            node_distribution = node_number / (node_number.sum(0).item())
   118→            self.nodes_distribution = node_distribution
   119→
   120→            # Compute the distribution of the edges
   121→            edge_number = torch.cat(edges).sum(0)  # (nbonds)
   122→            edge_distribution = edge_number / (edge_number.sum(0).item())
   123→            self.edges_distribution = edge_distribution
   124→
   125→            # Compute the distribution of number of nodes
   126→            num_atoms_dist = Counter([n.sum(-1).item() for n in nodes])
   127→            max_num_atom = max(num_atoms_dist.keys())
   128→            self.num_atoms_dist = torch.tensor(
   129→                [num_atoms_dist.get(i + 1, 0) / len(nodes) for i in range(max_num_atom)]
   130→            )
   131→
   132→            # Compute the maximum weight of the dataset
   133→            weight_tensor = torch.tensor(
   134→                [getattr(VALID_ELEMENTS[at], "weight") for at in self.valid_elements]
   135→            )
   136→            self.max_weight = max(
   137→                [
   138→                    (n_mat.float() @ weight_tensor.float()).sum().item()
   139→                    for n_mat in nodes
   140→                ]
   141→            )
   142→
   143→            # Save to cache only when we actually call _build not load from cache
   144→            if cache_path is not None and save_cache:
   145→                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(cache_path)), exist_ok=True)
   146→                if verbose:
   147→                    print(f"Saving dataset cache to: {cache_path}")
   148→                torch.save(
   149→                    {
   150→                        "smiles": self.smiles,
   151→                        "valid_elements": self.valid_elements,
   152→                        "nodes_distribution": self.nodes_distribution,
   153→                        "edges_distribution": self.edges_distribution,
   154→                        "num_atoms_dist": self.num_atoms_dist,
   155→                        "max_weight": self.max_weight,
   156→                    },
   157→                    cache_path,
   158→                )
   159→
   160→    def _build(
   161→        self,
   162→        smiles_list: list[str],
   163→        sanitizer: Callable | None,
   164→        verbose: bool,
   165→    ):
   166→        """Build graph representations and statistics from a list of SMILES strings."""
   167→        # Get the valid smiles, and compute node / edges distributions -> for noise schedule
   168→        smiles_nodes_edges = []
   169→        for sm in tqdm(smiles_list, desc="Building graph", disable=not verbose):
   170→            graph = self.smilesToGraph(sm)
   171→            if graph is None:
   172→                continue
   173→
   174→            nodes, edges = graph
   175→            # Sanitize checks
   176→            if sanitizer:
   177→                DisableLog("rdApp.*")
   178→                if not sanitizer(nodes, edges, valid_elements=self.valid_elements):
   179→                    continue
   180→
   181→            # Compute aggregated stats for distribution calculation later
   182→            # graph[0]=nodes, graph[1]=edges
   183→            smiles_nodes_edges.append(
   184→                (
   185→                    sm,
   186→                    nodes.sum(0).unsqueeze(0),
   187→                    edges.sum(0).sum(0).unsqueeze(0),
   188→                )
   189→            )
   190→
   191→        if sanitizer:
   192→            print(
   193→                f"Sanitizer removed {len(smiles_list) - len(smiles_nodes_edges)} molecules / {len(smiles_list)} molecules"
   194→            )
   195→
   196→        smiles, nodes, edges = zip(*smiles_nodes_edges)
   197→
   198→        return smiles, nodes, edges
   199→
   200→    def smilesToGraph(self, smiles: str) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None:
   201→        """
   202→        Convert a SMILES string into node and edge tensor representations.
   203→
   204→        Args:
   205→            smiles (str): The SMILES string to convert.
   206→
   207→        Returns:
   208→            tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None: A tuple (nodes, edges) if successful,
   209→                where nodes is of shape (n, natoms) and edges is of shape (n, n, nbonds).
   210→                Returns None if conversion fails or if the molecule contains invalid elements.
   211→        """
   212→
   213→        # Make a molecule
   214→        mol = Chem.MolFromSmiles(smiles)
   215→
   216→        # If rdkit is not able to make a molecule from the smile -> None
   217→        if mol is None:
   218→            return None
   219→
   220→        # Initialize the nodes, edges matrices
   221→        n = mol.GetNumAtoms()
   222→        nodes = torch.zeros((n, len(self.valid_elements)), dtype=int)  # (n, natoms)
   223→        edges = torch.zeros((n, n, len(TYPE_EDGES)), dtype=int)  # (n, n, nbonds)
   224→
   225→        for i, atom in enumerate(mol.GetAtoms()):
   226→            # Return None for the molecules that are not in the ones of interest
   227→            atom_symbol = atom.GetSymbol()
   228→            if atom_symbol not in self.valid_elements:
   229→                return None
   230→
   231→            # One-hot encode the atom
   232→            nodes[i, self.valid_elements.index(atom_symbol)] = 1
   233→
   234→            # Iter over the bonds of the atom
   235→            for bond in atom.GetBonds():
   236→                # TODO : check how this method works -> doubt that bond works sym
   237→                s = bond.GetBeginAtomIdx()
   238→                e = bond.GetEndAtomIdx()
   239→                bond_type = bond.GetBondType()
   240→
   241→                # Return None for the molecules with edges not in the ones of interest.
   242→                if bond_type not in TYPE_EDGES:
   243→                    return None
   244→
   245→                # One-hot encode the type of edge
   246→                edges[s, e, TYPE_EDGES.index(bond_type)] = 1
   247→
   248→        # Symmetrize the matrix
   249→        edges = edges + edges.transpose(0, 1)  # (n, natoms)
   250→
   251→        # One-hot encode the edges that have yet no 1 -> means no edges
   252→        mask = edges.sum(-1)
   253→        edges[:, :, 0] += 1 - mask  # Put a 0 at dim1 -> No Bond # (n, n, nbonds)
   254→
   255→        return nodes, edges
   256→
   257→    def graphToSmiles(self, nodes: torch.Tensor, edges: torch.Tensor) -> str:
   258→        """
   259→        Convert a graph representation back to a SMILES string.
   260→
   261→        Args:
   262→            nodes (torch.Tensor): One-hot encoded node features of shape (n, natoms).
   263→            edges (torch.Tensor): One-hot encoded edge features of shape (n, n, nbonds).
   264→
   265→        Returns:
   266→            str: The reconstructed SMILES string.
   267→        """
   268→        # Create a writable molecule
   269→        mol = Chem.RWMol()
   270→
   271→        # Add atoms
   272→        atom_indices = []
   273→        for i in range(nodes.shape[0]):
   274→            atom_idx = torch.argmax(nodes[i]).item()
   275→            atom_symbol = self.valid_elements[atom_idx]
   276→            atom = Chem.Atom(atom_symbol)
   277→            idx = mol.AddAtom(atom)
   278→            atom_indices.append(idx)
   279→
   280→        # Add bonds
   281→        # edges is (n, n, nbonds)
   282→        # We iterate over the upper triangle to avoid duplicates
   283→        n = nodes.shape[0]
   284→        for i in range(n):
   285→            for j in range(i + 1, n):
   286→                bond_type_idx = torch.argmax(edges[i, j]).item()
   287→                bond_type = TYPE_EDGES[bond_type_idx]
   288→
   289→                if bond_type != "NoBond":
   290→                    mol.AddBond(atom_indices[i], atom_indices[j], bond_type)
   291→
   292→        # Sanitize the molecule to handle aromaticity etc.
   293→        try:
   294→            Chem.SanitizeMol(mol)
   295→        except ValueError:
   296→            # If sanitization fails, we might return a raw SMILES or None
   297→            # For now let's try to return what we have, but it might be invalid
   298→            pass
   299→
   300→        # Convert to SMILES
   301→        smiles = Chem.MolToSmiles(mol)
   302→        return smiles
   303→
   304→    def __len__(self):
   305→        """
   306→        Get the number of molecules in the dataset.
   307→
   308→        Returns:
   309→            int: The number of SMILES strings in the dataset.
   310→        """
   311→        return len(self.smiles)
   312→
   313→    def __getitem__(self, idx):
   314→        """
   315→        Get a graph representation of a molecule by index.
   316→
   317→        Args:
   318→            idx (int): The index of the molecule to fetch.
   319→
   320→        Returns:
   321→            tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: A tuple (nodes, edges) containing:
   322→                - nodes (torch.Tensor): One-hot encoded nodes of shape (n, natoms).
   323→                - edges (torch.Tensor): One-hot encoded edges of shape (n, n, nbonds).
   324→        """
   325→        sm = self.smiles[idx]
   326→
   327→        # Calculate the nodes and edges
   328→        nodes, edges = self.smilesToGraph(sm)  # (n, natoms), (n, n, nbonds)
   329→
   330→        return nodes, edges
   331→

1→import torch
     2→from torch.nn.attention.flex_attention import create_block_mask
     3→from torch.nn.functional import pad
     4→from torch.nn.utils.rnn import pad_sequence
     5→
     6→
     7→def collateGraph(
     8→    batch: list[tuple[torch.Tensor]],
     9→):
    10→    """
    11→    Data collate function to transform the outputs of the dataset into batches
    12→    that will be fed to the DataLoader objects during the training.
    13→    This function is made to be used with the GraphDatasetFromSMILEs object and
    14→    plug it to a torch DataLoader.
    15→
    16→    Args:
    17→    batch, which is a list of size 3 tuples made of :
    18→    - N: torch.Tensor, contains node of size (n_mol, natoms)
    19→    - E: torch.Tensor, contains edge of size (n_mol, n_mol, nbonds)
    20→    - pos_emb: torch.Tensor, contains pos_emb (n_mol, k)
    21→
    22→    Returns:
    23→    tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: A tuple containing:
    24→    - nodes: torch.Tensor of shape (bs, n_batch, natoms)
    25→    - edges: torch.Tensor of shape (bs, n_batch, n_batch, nbonds)
    26→    - mask: torch.Tensor of shape (bs, n_batch)
    27→    """
    28→    # Unpack the nodes, edges and pos_emb
    29→    # bs = len(batch)
    30→    list_N, list_E = zip(*batch)
    31→
    32→    # Look at the number of atoms in each graph
    33→    num_atoms = [N.shape[0] for N in list_N]
    34→    n_batch = max(num_atoms)
    35→
    36→    # Pad the nodes
    37→    N_padded = (
    38→        pad_sequence(list_N).transpose(0, 1).to(torch.float32)
    39→    )  # (bs, n_batch, natoms)
    40→
    41→    # Pad the edges
    42→    E_padded = torch.cat(
    43→        [
    44→            pad(E, (0, 0, 0, n_batch - n, 0, n_batch - n)).unsqueeze(0)
    45→            for n, E in zip(num_atoms, list_E)
    46→        ],
    47→        dim=0,
    48→    ).to(torch.float32)  # (bs, n_batch, n_batch, k)
    49→
    50→    # Make the mask
    51→    mask = torch.stack(
    52→        [torch.cat([torch.ones(m), torch.zeros(n_batch - m)]) for m in num_atoms]
    53→    )  # (bs, n_batch)
    54→
    55→    return N_padded, E_padded, mask
    56→
    57→
    58→def collateGraphJagged(batch: list[tuple[torch.Tensor]]):
    59→    # Collate the nodes and edges in a jagged way (nested tensors).
    60→    # We will end with a dimensions :
    61→    # - L -> total number of nodes of the batch
    62→    # - M -> total number of edges of the batch
    63→    list_N, list_E = zip(*batch)
    64→
    65→    # Look at the number of atoms in each graph
    66→    graph_id = torch.hstack(
    67→        [torch.tensor([i for _ in range(N.shape[0])]) for i, N in enumerate(list_N)]
    68→    )  # (L,)
    69→    num_tokens = graph_id.shape[0]
    70→
    71→    # Make the block mask
    72→    def causal(b, h, q_idx, kv_idx):
    73→        q_bs = graph_id[q_idx]
    74→        kv_bs = graph_id[kv_idx]
    75→
    76→        return q_bs == kv_bs
    77→
    78→    block_mask = create_block_mask(
    79→        causal, B=None, H=None, Q_LEN=num_tokens, KV_LEN=num_tokens
    80→    )  # (..., ..., L, L)
    81→
    82→    # Stack the nodes and edges
    83→    N_jagged = torch.vstack(list_N).unsqueeze(0)  # (1, L, n_nodes)
    84→    E_jagged = torch.vstack(list_E).unsqueeze(0)  # (1, M, n_nodes)
    85→
    86→    return N_jagged, E_jagged
    87→
    88→
    89→def collateGraphStatic(
    90→    batch: list[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]],
    91→    n_max: int,
    92→):
    93→    """
    94→    Data collate function to transform the outputs of the dataset into batches
    95→    with a static shape (n_max).
    96→
    97→    Args:
    98→    batch, which is a list of size 2 tuples made of :
    99→    - N: torch.Tensor, contains node of size (n_mol, natoms)
   100→    - E: torch.Tensor, contains edge of size (n_mol, n_mol, nbonds)
   101→    n_max: int, the fixed number of nodes to pad to.
   102→
   103→    Returns:
   104→    tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: A tuple containing:
   105→    - nodes: torch.Tensor of shape (bs, n_max, natoms)
   106→    - edges: torch.Tensor of shape (bs, n_max, n_max, nbonds)
   107→    - mask: torch.Tensor of shape (bs, n_max)
   108→    """
   109→    list_N, list_E = zip(*batch)
   110→
   111→    # Pad the nodes
   112→    N_padded = torch.stack(
   113→        [pad(N, (0, 0, 0, n_max - N.shape[0])).to(torch.float32) for N in list_N]
   114→    )  # (bs, n_max, natoms)
   115→
   116→    # Pad the edges
   117→    E_padded = torch.stack(
   118→        [
   119→            pad(E, (0, 0, 0, n_max - E.shape[0], 0, n_max - E.shape[0])).to(
   120→                torch.float32
   121→            )
   122→            for E in list_E
   123→        ]
   124→    )  # (bs, n_max, n_max, nbonds)
   125→
   126→    # Make the mask
   127→    mask = torch.stack(
   128→        [
   129→            torch.cat([torch.ones(N.shape[0]), torch.zeros(n_max - N.shape[0])])
   130→            for N in list_N
   131→        ]
   132→    )  # (bs, n_max)
   133→
   134→    return N_padded, E_padded, mask
   135→

     4→from collections import Counter
     5→from typing import Callable

     7→import pandas as pd
     8→import rdkit.Chem as Chem
     9→import torch
    10→from pandas.core.frame import DataFrame
    11→from rdkit.RDLogger import DisableLog
    12→from torch.utils.data import Dataset
    13→from tqdm import tqdm

    15→from annotix_ml.graphtransf.data.atoms_data import TYPE_EDGES, VALID_ELEMENTS

    17→from annotix_ml.spectraencoder.data.objects import Spectra

    20→def _extract_atoms_from_smiles(smiles_list: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    21→    atoms = set()
    22→    for smiles in smiles_list:
    23→        mol = Chem.MolFromSmiles(smiles)
    24→        if mol is not None:
    25→            for atom in mol.GetAtoms():
    26→                atoms.add(atom.GetSymbol())
    27→    return sorted(list(atoms))
    28→
    29→
    30→class GraphSpecDataset(Dataset):
    31→    """
    32→    GraphSpecDataset combines molecular graph transformation from SMILES
    33→    and MS2 spectra transformation from associated files.
    34→    """
    35→
    36→    def __init__(
    37→        self,
    38→        data: str | DataFrame,
    39→        spec_folder: str | Path,
    40→        subform_folder: str | Path,
    41→        smile_column: str = "smiles",
    42→        spec_column: str = "spec",
    43→        formula_column: str = "formula",
    44→        instrument_column: str = "instrument",
    45→        valid_elements: list[str] | None = None,
    46→        sanitizer: Callable | None = None,
    47→        verbose: bool = True,
    48→        cache_path: str | None = None,
    49→        save_cache: bool = True,
    50→        **kwargs,
    51→    ):
    52→        super().__init__()
    53→        if isinstance(data, (str, Path)):
    54→            self.data = pd.read_csv(
    55→                data, sep="\t" if str(data).endswith(".tsv") else ","
    56→            )
    57→        else:
    58→            self.data = data
    59→
    60→        self.spec_folder = Path(spec_folder)
    61→        self.subform_folder = Path(subform_folder)
    62→        self.smile_column = smile_column
    63→        self.spec_column = spec_column
    64→        self.formula_column = formula_column
    65→        self.instrument_column = instrument_column
    66→
    67→        # SMILES list
    68→        smiles_list = self.data[smile_column].to_list()
    69→
    70→        # Valid elements for graph
    71→        if valid_elements is None:
    72→            self.valid_elements = _extract_atoms_from_smiles(smiles_list)
    73→        else:
    74→            self.valid_elements = valid_elements
    75→
    76→        # Spectra featurizer
    77→        self.spec_featurizer = PeakFormula(subform_folder=str(subform_folder), **kwargs)
    78→
    79→        # Try to load from cache if a cache path is provided
    80→        if cache_path is not None and os.path.isfile(cache_path):
    81→            print(f"Loading dataset from cache: {cache_path}")
    82→            cache = torch.load(cache_path, weights_only=False)
    83→            self.smiles = cache["smiles"]
    84→            self.spec_names = cache["spec_names"]
    85→            self.formulas = cache["formulas"]
    86→            self.instruments = cache["instruments"]
    87→            self.valid_elements = cache["valid_elements"]
    88→            self.nodes_distribution = cache["nodes_distribution"]
    89→            self.edges_distribution = cache["edges_distribution"]
    90→            self.num_atoms_dist = cache["num_atoms_dist"]
    91→            self.max_weight = cache["max_weight"]
    92→
    93→        else:
    94→            smiles, spec_names, formulas, instruments, nodes, edges = self._build(
    95→                sanitizer, verbose
    96→            )
    97→            self.smiles = smiles
    98→            self.spec_names = spec_names
    99→            self.formulas = formulas
   100→            self.instruments = instruments
   101→
   102→            # Compute the distribution of nodes
   103→            node_number = torch.cat(nodes).sum(0)
   104→            self.nodes_distribution = node_number / (node_number.sum(0).item() + 1e-9)
   105→
   106→            # Compute the distribution of edges
   107→            edge_number = torch.cat(edges).sum(0)
   108→            self.edges_distribution = edge_number / (edge_number.sum(0).item() + 1e-9)
   109→
   110→            # Compute the distribution of number of nodes
   111→            num_atoms_dist = Counter([n.sum(-1).item() for n in nodes])
   112→            max_num_atom = max(num_atoms_dist.keys()) if num_atoms_dist else 0
   113→            self.num_atoms_dist = torch.tensor(
   114→                [num_atoms_dist.get(i + 1, 0) / len(nodes) for i in range(max_num_atom)]
   115→            )
   116→
   117→            # Compute the maximum weight of the dataset
   118→            weight_tensor = torch.tensor(
   119→                [getattr(VALID_ELEMENTS[at], "weight") for at in self.valid_elements]
   120→            )
   121→            self.max_weight = max(
   122→                [
   123→                    (n_mat.float() @ weight_tensor.float()).sum().item()
   124→                    for n_mat in nodes
   125→                ]
   126→            )
   127→
   128→            # Save to cache (only if requested, e.g. main rank in distributed mode)
   129→            if cache_path is not None and save_cache:
   130→                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(cache_path)), exist_ok=True)
   131→                print(f"Saving dataset cache to: {cache_path}")
   132→                torch.save(
   133→                    {
   134→                        "smiles": self.smiles,
   135→                        "spec_names": self.spec_names,
   136→                        "formulas": self.formulas,
   137→                        "instruments": self.instruments,
   138→                        "valid_elements": self.valid_elements,
   139→                        "nodes_distribution": self.nodes_distribution,
   140→                        "edges_distribution": self.edges_distribution,
   141→                        "num_atoms_dist": self.num_atoms_dist,
   142→                        "max_weight": self.max_weight,
   143→                    },
   144→                    cache_path,
   145→                )
   146→
   147→    def _build(self, sanitizer: Callable | None, verbose: bool):
   148→        smiles_nodes_edges = []
   149→        for _, row in tqdm(
   150→            self.data.iterrows(),
   151→            total=len(self.data),
   152→            desc="Processing dataset",
   153→            disable=not verbose,
   154→        ):
   155→            sm = row[self.smile_column]
   156→            graph = self.smilesToGraph(sm)
   157→            if graph is None:
   158→                continue
   159→
   160→            nodes, edges = graph
   161→            # Sanitize checks
   162→            if sanitizer:
   163→                DisableLog("rdApp.*")
   164→                if not sanitizer(nodes, edges, valid_elements=self.valid_elements):
   165→                    continue
   166→
   167→            # Check if spectra exists
   168→            spec_name = row[self.spec_column]
   169→            spec_file = self.spec_folder / f"{spec_name}.ms"
   170→            if not spec_file.exists():
   171→                logging.warning(f"Spec file {spec_file} not found, skipping.")
   172→                continue
   173→
   174→            smiles_nodes_edges.append(
   175→                (
   176→                    sm,
   177→                    spec_name,
   178→                    row.get(self.formula_column, ""),
   179→                    row.get(self.instrument_column, ""),
   180→                    nodes.sum(0).unsqueeze(0),
   181→                    edges.sum(0).sum(0).unsqueeze(0),
   182→                )
   183→            )
   184→
   185→        if not smiles_nodes_edges:
   186→            raise ValueError("No valid SMILES/Spectra pairs found in the dataset.")
   187→
   188→        smiles, spec_names, formulas, instruments, nodes, edges = zip(
   189→            *smiles_nodes_edges
   190→        )
   191→
   192→        return smiles, spec_names, formulas, instruments, nodes, edges
   193→
   194→    def smilesToGraph(self, smiles: str) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None:
   195→        mol = Chem.MolFromSmiles(smiles)
   196→        if mol is None:
   197→            return None
   198→
   199→        n = mol.GetNumAtoms()
   200→        nodes = torch.zeros((n, len(self.valid_elements)), dtype=int)
   201→        edges = torch.zeros((n, n, len(TYPE_EDGES)), dtype=int)
   202→
   203→        for i, atom in enumerate(mol.GetAtoms()):
   204→            atom_symbol = atom.GetSymbol()
   205→            if atom_symbol not in self.valid_elements:
   206→                return None
   207→            nodes[i, self.valid_elements.index(atom_symbol)] = 1
   208→
   209→            for bond in atom.GetBonds():
   210→                s = bond.GetBeginAtomIdx()
   211→                e = bond.GetEndAtomIdx()
   212→                bond_type = bond.GetBondType()
   213→                if bond_type not in TYPE_EDGES:
   214→                    return None
   215→                edges[s, e, TYPE_EDGES.index(bond_type)] = 1
   216→
   217→        edges = edges + edges.transpose(0, 1)
   218→        mask = edges.sum(-1)
   219→        edges[:, :, 0] += 1 - mask
   220→        return nodes, edges
   221→
   222→    def __len__(self):
   223→        return len(self.smiles)
   224→
   225→    def __getitem__(self, idx):
   226→        sm = self.smiles[idx]
   227→        spec_name = self.spec_names[idx]
   228→        formula = self.formulas[idx]
   229→        instrument = self.instruments[idx]
   230→
   231→        # Graph
   232→        nodes, edges = self.smilesToGraph(sm)
   233→
   234→        # Spectra
   235→        spec_obj = Spectra(
   236→            spectra_name=spec_name,
   237→            spectra_file=str(self.spec_folder / f"{spec_name}.ms"),
   238→            spectra_formula=formula,
   239→            instrument=instrument,
   240→        )
   241→        spec_features = self.spec_featurizer.featurize(spec_obj)
   242→
   243→        # Return merged dict
   244→        res = {"nodes": nodes, "edges": edges, "smiles": sm, "spec_name": spec_name}
   245→        res.update(spec_features)
   246→        return res

1→from typing import List
     2→import torch
     3→from annotix_ml.spectraencoder.data.featurizers import PeakFormula
     4→
     5→
     6→def graph_spec_collate_fn(batch: List[dict]) -> tuple:
     7→    """
     8→    Collate function for GraphSpecDataset.
     9→    Handles graph padding and spectra feature collation.
    10→
    11→    Returns:
    12→        tuple: (nodes, edges, mask, num_peaks, types, instruments, ion_vec, form_vec, intens, smiles)
    13→    """
    14→    # Collate spectra features using PeakFormula.collate_fn logic
    15→    spec_batch = PeakFormula.collate_fn(batch)
    16→
    17→    # Collate graph features
    18→    # Since nodes and edges have different sizes (N), we need padding
    19→    node_tensors = [d["nodes"] for d in batch]
    20→    edge_tensors = [d["edges"] for d in batch]
    21→
    22→    num_nodes = torch.tensor([n.shape[0] for n in node_tensors])
    23→    max_n = num_nodes.max()
    24→
    25→    padded_nodes = []
    26→    padded_edges = []
    27→    node_masks = []
    28→
    29→    for n, e in zip(node_tensors, edge_tensors):
    30→        curr_n = n.shape[0]
    31→        # Nodes: (n, natoms) -> (max_n, natoms)
    32→        padded_n = torch.nn.functional.pad(n, (0, 0, 0, max_n - curr_n))
    33→        padded_nodes.append(padded_n)
    34→
    35→        # Edges: (n, n, nbonds) -> (max_n, max_n, nbonds)
    36→        padded_e = torch.nn.functional.pad(
    37→            e, (0, 0, 0, max_n - curr_n, 0, max_n - curr_n)
    38→        )
    39→        # Set NoBond (index 0) for padded areas
    40→        padded_e[curr_n:, :, 0] = 1
    41→        padded_e[:, curr_n:, 0] = 1
    42→        padded_edges.append(padded_e)
    43→
    44→        mask = torch.zeros(max_n, dtype=torch.bool)
    45→        mask[:curr_n] = True
    46→        node_masks.append(mask)
    47→
    48→    nodes = torch.stack(padded_nodes).to(torch.float32)
    49→    edges = torch.stack(padded_edges).to(torch.float32)
    50→    mask = torch.stack(node_masks)
    51→    smiles = [d["smiles"] for d in batch]
    52→
    53→    return (
    54→        nodes,
    55→        edges,
    56→        mask,
    57→        spec_batch["num_peaks"],
    58→        spec_batch["types"],
    59→        spec_batch["instruments"],
    60→        spec_batch["ion_vec"],
    61→        spec_batch["form_vec"],
    62→        spec_batch["intens"],
    63→        smiles,
    64→    )

     6→def mask_any_tensor(
     7→    t: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor, fill: float = 0.0
     8→) -> torch.Tensor:
     9→    """Apply a 0/1 mask to the leading dimensions of a tensor, filling masked
    10→    positions with a scalar value.
    11→
    12→    The function expects ``mask`` to have shape equal to the leading (left-most)
    13→    dimensions of ``t``. Any remaining trailing dimensions of ``t`` are treated
    14→    as feature dimensions and the mask is expanded (unsqueezed) over them.
    15→
    16→    Behavior summary
    17→    - If ``mask.shape == t.shape[:len(mask.shape)]`` the mask is unsqueezed
    18→      for each remaining trailing dimension of ``t`` and then applied.
    19→    - Positions where ``mask == 0`` are replaced by ``fill`` via
    20→      :meth:`torch.Tensor.masked_fill`.
    21→    - Non-zero mask values are treated as keep indicators.
    22→
    23→    Args:
    24→        t: Input tensor to mask. Any dtype is supported; ``fill`` will be
    25→           cast as needed by PyTorch when filling.
    26→        mask: Binary (0/1) or boolean tensor whose shape must match the leading
    27→           dimensions of ``t``. For example, if ``t`` has shape
    28→           ``(B, N, F)`` then ``mask`` can be ``(B, N)`` or ``(B, N, 1)``.
    29→        fill: Scalar value used to fill masked locations (where ``mask == 0``).
    30→
    31→    Returns:
    32→        A tensor of the same shape and dtype as ``t`` with masked positions
    33→        replaced by ``fill``.
    34→
    35→    Example:
    36→        >>> t = torch.tensor([[[1., 2.], [3., 4.]], [[5., 6.], [7., 8.]]])
    37→        >>> mask = torch.tensor([[1, 0], [0, 1]])
    38→        >>> mask_any_tensor(t, mask, fill=0.0)
    39→        tensor([[[1., 2.],
    40→                 [0., 0.]],
    41→
    42→                [[0., 0.],
    43→                 [7., 8.]]])
    44→
    45→    Notes and edge cases:
    46→    - The function asserts that ``mask.shape`` equals the leading dimensions of
    47→      ``t``; a mismatch will raise an AssertionError.
    48→    - ``mask`` may be integer or boolean. Zeros are considered masked.
    49→    - Time/space complexity is linear in the number of elements in ``t``.
    50→
    51→    """
    52→    while mask.dim() < t.dim():
    53→        mask = mask.unsqueeze(-1)
    54→
    55→    return t.masked_fill(~mask.bool(), fill)

    58→def mol_to_smiles(mol):

    66→def graph_to_mol(nodes, edges, valid_elements):
    67→    n_atoms = nodes.shape[0]
    68→    # Create a writable molecule
    69→    mol = Chem.RWMol()

    71→    # Add atoms
    72→    atom_indices = []

    75→        atom_symbol = valid_elements[atom_idx]
    76→        atom = Chem.Atom(atom_symbol)
    77→        idx = mol.AddAtom(atom)
    78→        atom_indices.append(idx)
    79→
    80→    # Add bonds
    81→    # Iterate over the upper triangle to avoid duplicates
    82→
    83→    for j in range(n_atoms):
    84→        for k in range(j + 1, n_atoms):
    85→            bond_type_idx = torch.argmax(edges[j, k]).item()

    98→def auto_fix_kekulization(smiles):

   106→        ^ Chem.SanitizeFlags.SANITIZE_SETAROMATICITY,

   125→        try:

   130→            n.SetNumExplicitHs(0)

   138→    nodes: torch.Tensor,

   141→) -> str | None:

   144→
   145→    Args:
   146→    - nodes: torch.Tensor, one-hot encoded nodes (natoms)
   147→    - edges: torch.Tensor, one-hot encoded edges (natoms, natoms, nbonds)

   150→    Returns:
   151→    - smiles: str | None, reconstructed SMILES string. None if invalid.
   152→    """
   153→    # Create a writable molecule
   154→    mol = graph_to_mol(nodes, edges, valid_elements)
   155→
   156→    # Sanitize the molecule
   157→    smiles = None
   158→    try:
   159→        Chem.SanitizeMol(mol)
   160→        smiles = Chem.MolToSmiles(mol)
   161→    except Exception:
   162→        try:
   163→            Chem.SanitizeMol(
   164→                mol,
   165→                Chem.SanitizeFlags.SANITIZE_ALL ^ Chem.SanitizeFlags.SANITIZE_KEKULIZE,
   166→            )
   167→            smiles = Chem.MolToSmiles(mol)
   168→        except Exception:
   169→            pass
   170→
   171→    if smiles is None:
   172→        return None
   173→
   174→    mol = Chem.MolFromSmiles(smiles)
   175→
   176→    if mol:
   177→        smiles = Chem.MolToSmiles(mol)
   178→    else:
   179→        try:
   180→            mol = auto_fix_kekulization(smiles)
   181→            smiles = Chem.MolToSmiles(mol)

1→import itertools
     2→from typing import Any
     3→
     4→import torch
     5→from torch.utils.data.sampler import Sampler
     6→
     7→import annotix_ml.distributed as distributed
     8→
     9→
    10→def _get_torch_dtype(size: int) -> Any:
    11→    return torch.int32 if size <= 2**31 else torch.int64
    12→
    13→
    14→def _generate_randperm_indices(*, size: int, generator: torch.Generator):
    15→    """Generate the indices of a random permutation."""
    16→    dtype = _get_torch_dtype(size)
    17→    # This is actually matching PyTorch's CPU implementation, see: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/aten/src/ATen/native/TensorFactories.cpp#L900-L921
    18→    perm = torch.arange(size, dtype=dtype)
    19→    for i in range(size):
    20→        j = torch.randint(i, size, size=(1,), generator=generator).item()
    21→
    22→        # Always swap even if no-op
    23→        value = perm[j].item()
    24→        perm[j] = perm[i].item()
    25→        perm[i] = value
    26→        yield value
    27→
    28→
    29→class InfiniteSampler(Sampler):
    30→    def __init__(
    31→        self,
    32→        *,
    33→        sample_count: int,
    34→        shuffle: bool = False,
    35→        seed: int = 0,
    36→        start: int | None = None,
    37→        step: int | None = None,
    38→        advance: int = 0,
    39→    ):
    40→        self._sample_count = sample_count
    41→        self._seed = seed
    42→        self._shuffle = shuffle
    43→
    44→        # If start or step is provided, use it.
    45→        # Otherwise, fallback to distributed global rank/size for data parallelism.
    46→        if start is None:
    47→            start = distributed.get_global_rank()
    48→        if step is None:
    49→            step = distributed.get_global_size()
    50→
    51→        self._start = start
    52→        self._step = step
    53→        self._advance = advance
    54→
    55→    def __iter__(self):
    56→        if self._shuffle:
    57→            iterator = self._shuffled_iterator()
    58→        else:
    59→            iterator = self._iterator()
    60→
    61→        yield from itertools.islice(iterator, self._advance, None)
    62→
    63→    def _iterator(self):
    64→        assert not self._shuffle
    65→
    66→        while True:
    67→            iterable = range(self._sample_count)
    68→            yield from itertools.islice(iterable, self._start, None, self._step)
    69→
    70→    def _shuffled_iterator(self):
    71→        assert self._shuffle
    72→
    73→        # Instantiate a generator here (rather than in the ctor) to keep the class
    74→        # picklable (requirement of mp.spawn)
    75→        generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(self._seed)
    76→
    77→        while True:
    78→            iterable = _generate_randperm_indices(
    79→                size=self._sample_count, generator=generator
    80→            )
    81→            yield from itertools.islice(iterable, self._start, None, self._step)
    82→

1→"""modules.py"""
     2→
     3→import copy
     4→import torch
     5→import numpy as np
     6→from torch import nn
     7→
     8→from annotix_ml.spectraencoder.utils import max_instr_idx as MAX_INSTR_IDX
     9→from annotix_ml.spectraencoder.model.transformer_layer import TransformerEncoderLayer
    10→from annotix_ml.spectraencoder.model.form_embedders import get_embedder
    11→

    13→EPS = 1e-9
    14→

    16→def get_num_inten_feats(inten_transform):
    17→    if inten_transform == "float":
    18→        inten_feats = 1
    19→    elif inten_transform == "zero":
    20→        inten_feats = 1
    21→    elif inten_transform == "log":
    22→        inten_feats = 1
    23→    elif inten_transform == "cat":

    25→    else:

    30→class MLPBlocks(nn.Module):
    31→    def __init__(
    32→        self,
    33→        input_size: int,
    34→        hidden_size: int,
    35→        dropout: float,
    36→        num_layers: int,
    37→    ):
    38→        super().__init__()
    39→        self.activation = nn.ReLU()
    40→        self.dropout_layer = nn.Dropout(p=dropout)
    41→        self.input_layer = nn.Linear(input_size, hidden_size)
    42→        middle_layer = nn.Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size)
    43→        self.layers = _get_clones(middle_layer, num_layers - 1)
    44→
    45→    def forward(self, x):
    46→        output = x
    47→        output = self.input_layer(x)
    48→        output = self.dropout_layer(output)
    49→        output = self.activation(output)
    50→        for layer_index, layer in enumerate(self.layers):
    51→            output = layer(output)
    52→            output = self.dropout_layer(output)
    53→            output = self.activation(output)
    54→        return output

    57→class FormulaTransformer(nn.Module):
    58→    """FormulaTransformer"""
    59→
    60→    def __init__(
    61→        self,
    62→        hidden_size: int,
    63→        peak_attn_layers: int,
    64→        set_pooling: str = "intensity",
    65→        spectra_dropout: float = 0.1,
    66→        pairwise_featurization: bool = False,
    67→        num_heads: int = 8,
    68→        output_size=2048,
    69→        form_embedder: str = "float",
    70→        embed_instrument: bool = False,
    71→        inten_transform: str = "float",
    72→        no_diffs: bool = False,
    73→    ):
    74→        """_summary_
    75→        Args:
    76→                    hidden_size (int): _description_
    77→                    peak_attn_layers (int): _description_
    78→                    set_pooling (str, optional): _description_. Defaults to "intensity".
    79→                        intensity: Weight by intensity of each chem formula
    80→                        root: Only take the root node
    81→                        cls: Only take at first class node
    82→                        mean: Take the mean of all nodes
    83→                    spectra_dropout (float, optional): _description_. Defaults to 0.1.
    84→                    pairwise_featurization (bool, optional): _description_. Defaults to False.
    85→                    num_heads (int, optional): _description_. Defaults to 8.
    86→                    output_size (int, optional): _description_. Defaults to 2048.
    87→                    form_embedder (str, optional): _description_. Defaults to "float".
    88→                    embed_instrument (bool, optional): _description_. Defaults to False.
    89→                    inten_transform (str, optional): _description_. Defaults to "float".
    90→                    no_diffs (str): If true, do not use diff representations
    91→
    92→                Raises:
    93→                    ValueError: _description_
    94→        """
    95→        nn.Module.__init__(self)
    96→        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
    97→        self.attn_heads = num_heads
    98→        self.dim_feedforward = self.hidden_size * 4
    99→        self.spectra_dropout = spectra_dropout
   100→        self.set_pooling = set_pooling
   101→        self.output_size = output_size
   102→        self.no_diffs = no_diffs
   103→
   104→        self.form_embedder = form_embedder
   105→        self.form_embedder_mod = get_embedder(self.form_embedder)
   106→
   107→        self.embed_instrument = embed_instrument
   108→        self.instr_dim = MAX_INSTR_IDX
   109→        self.instrument_embedder = nn.Parameter(torch.eye(self.instr_dim))
   110→
   111→        self.inten_transform = inten_transform
   112→        ########### CHANGED FROM ORIGINAL IMPLEMENTATION ############
   113→        self.inten_feats = get_num_inten_feats(self.inten_transform)
   114→        self.num_types = 4
   115→        self.cls_type = 3
   116→
   117→        self.adduct_dim = 8
   118→        ############### END OF CHANGES ###############################
   119→
   120→        self.pairwise_featurization = pairwise_featurization
   121→
   122→        # Define dense encoders and root formula encoder
   123→        self.formula_dim = self.form_embedder_mod.full_dim
   124→        self.input_dim = (
   125→            self.formula_dim * 2
   126→            + self.num_types
   127→            + self.instr_dim
   128→            + self.inten_feats
   129→            + self.adduct_dim
   130→        )
   131→
   132→        self.intermediate_layer = MLPBlocks(
   133→            input_size=self.input_dim,
   134→            hidden_size=self.hidden_size,
   135→            dropout=self.spectra_dropout,
   136→            num_layers=2,
   137→        )
   138→        self.pairwise_featurizer = None
   139→        if self.pairwise_featurization:
   140→            self.pairwise_featurizer = MLPBlocks(
   141→                input_size=self.formula_dim,
   142→                hidden_size=self.hidden_size,
   143→                dropout=self.spectra_dropout,
   144→                num_layers=2,
   145→            )
   146→
   147→        # Multihead attention block with residuals
   148→        peak_attn_layer = TransformerEncoderLayer(
   149→            d_model=self.hidden_size,
   150→            nhead=self.attn_heads,
   151→            dim_feedforward=self.dim_feedforward,
   152→            dropout=self.spectra_dropout,
   153→            pairwise_featurization=pairwise_featurization,
   154→        )
   155→        self.peak_attn_layers = _get_clones(peak_attn_layer, peak_attn_layers)
   156→        self.bin_encoder = None
   157→
   158→    def forward(self, batch: dict, return_aux=False):
   159→        """forward."""
   160→        # Step 1: Create embeddings
   161→        num_peaks = batch["num_peaks"]
   162→        peak_types = batch["types"]
   163→        instruments = batch["instruments"]
   164→
   165→        device = num_peaks.device
   166→        batch_dim = num_peaks.shape[0]
   167→        peak_dim = peak_types.shape[-1]
   168→        adducts = batch["ion_vec"]
   169→
   170→        cls_token_mask = peak_types == self.cls_type
   171→
   172→        # Get form vec and get diffs
   173→        orig_form_vec = batch["form_vec"][:, :, :]
   174→        form_diffs = orig_form_vec[:, :, None, :] - orig_form_vec[:, None, :, :]
   175→
   176→        # Embed formulae based upon peak type
   177→        abs_diffs = form_diffs[cls_token_mask]
   178→        form_vec = self.form_embedder_mod(orig_form_vec)
   179→        diff_vec = self.form_embedder_mod(abs_diffs)  # .fill_(0)
   180→
   181→        if self.no_diffs:
   182→            diff_vec = diff_vec.fill_(0)
   183→
   184→        intens_temp = batch["intens"]
   185→
   186→        if self.inten_transform == "cat":
   187→            inten_tensor = torch.eye(self.num_inten_bins + 1, device=device)[
   188→                intens_temp.long()
   189→            ]
   190→        else:
   191→            inten_tensor = intens_temp[:, :, None]
   192→
   193→        one_hot_types = nn.functional.one_hot(peak_types, self.num_types)
   194→        one_hot_adducts = nn.functional.one_hot(adducts.long(), self.adduct_dim)
   195→
   196→        embedded_instruments = self.instrument_embedder[instruments.long()]
   197→        if self.embed_instrument:
   198→            embedded_instruments = embedded_instruments[:, None, :].repeat(
   199→                1, peak_dim, 1
   200→            )
   201→        else:
   202→            embedded_instruments = torch.zeros(batch_dim, peak_dim, self.instr_dim).to(
   203→                device
   204→            )
   205→
   206→        input_vec = [
   207→            form_vec,
   208→            diff_vec,
   209→            one_hot_types,
   210→            one_hot_adducts,
   211→            inten_tensor,
   212→            embedded_instruments,
   213→        ]
   214→        input_vec = torch.cat(input_vec, dim=-1)
   215→        peak_tensor = self.intermediate_layer(input_vec)
   216→
   217→        # Step 3: Run transformer
   218→        # B x Np x d -> Np x B x d
   219→        peak_tensor = peak_tensor.transpose(0, 1)
   220→        # Mask before summing
   221→        peak_dim = peak_tensor.shape[0]
   222→        peaks_aranged = torch.arange(peak_dim).to(device)
   223→
   224→        # batch x num peaks
   225→        attn_mask = ~(peaks_aranged[None, :] < num_peaks[:, None])
   226→        pairwise_features = None
   227→        if self.pairwise_featurization:
   228→            # Make sure to _only_ consider subset fragments, rather than only
   229→            # partial additions/subtractions from across the tree branches
   230→            # Comment out to consider _any_ loss embedding with new parameters
   231→            same_sign = torch.all(form_diffs >= 0, -1) | torch.all(form_diffs <= 0, -1)
   232→            form_diffs[~same_sign].fill_(0)
   233→            form_diffs = torch.abs(form_diffs)
   234→            pairwise_features = self.pairwise_featurizer(
   235→                self.form_embedder_mod(form_diffs)
   236→            )
   237→
   238→        # Np x B x d
   239→        aux_output = {}
   240→        for peak_attn_layer in self.peak_attn_layers:
   241→            peak_tensor, pairwise_features = peak_attn_layer(
   242→                peak_tensor,
   243→                pairwise_features=pairwise_features,
   244→                src_key_padding_mask=attn_mask,
   245→            )
   246→
   247→        # Step 4: Pool output
   248→        output, peak_tensor = self._pool_out(
   249→            peak_tensor, inten_tensor, peak_types, attn_mask, batch_dim
   250→        )
   251→        aux_output["peak_tensor"] = peak_tensor.transpose(0, 1)
   252→
   253→        # Now convert into output dim
   254→        if return_aux:
   255→            output = (output, aux_output)
   256→
   257→        return output
   258→
   259→    def _pool_out(self, peak_tensor, inten_tensor, peak_types, attn_mask, batch_dim):
   260→        """_pool_out.
   261→
   262→        pool the output of the network
   263→
   264→        Return:
   265→            (output (B x H), peak_tensor : L x B x H)
   266→
   267→        """
   268→
   269→        #  Np x B x d
   270→        zero_mask = attn_mask[:, :, None].repeat(1, 1, self.hidden_size).transpose(0, 1)
   271→
   272→        # Mask over NaN
   273→        peak_tensor[zero_mask] = 0
   274→        # if torch.any(num_peaks == 0).item():
   275→        #    raise ValueError("Unexpected example with zero peaks")
   276→        if self.set_pooling == "intensity":
   277→            inten_tensor = inten_tensor.reshape(batch_dim, -1)
   278→            intensities_sum = inten_tensor.sum(1).reshape(-1, 1) + EPS
   279→            inten_tensor = inten_tensor / intensities_sum
   280→            pool_factor = inten_tensor * ~attn_mask
   281→        elif self.set_pooling == "mean":
   282→            inten_tensor = inten_tensor.reshape(batch_dim, -1)
   283→            pool_factor = torch.clone(inten_tensor).fill_(1)
   284→            pool_factor = pool_factor * ~attn_mask
   285→            # Replace all zeros with 1
   286→            pool_factor[pool_factor == 0] = 1
   287→            pool_factor = pool_factor / pool_factor.sum(1).reshape(-1, 1)
   288→        elif self.set_pooling == "root":
   289→            # Reshape to have batch dim, -1
   290→            inten_tensor = inten_tensor.reshape(batch_dim, -1)
   291→            pool_factor = torch.zeros_like(inten_tensor)
   292→            pool_factor[:, 0] = 1
   293→        elif self.set_pooling == "cls":
   294→            pool_factor = (peak_types == self.cls_type).float()
   295→        else:
   296→            raise NotImplementedError()
   297→
   298→        # Weighted average over peak intensities
   299→        output = torch.einsum("nbd,bn->bd", peak_tensor, pool_factor)
   300→        return output, peak_tensor
   301→
   302→
   303→class FPGrowingModule(nn.Module):
   304→    """FPGrowingModule.
   305→
   306→    Accept an input hidden dim and progressively grow by powers of 2 s.t.
   307→
   308→    We eventually get to the final output size...
   309→
   310→    """
   311→
   312→    def __init__(
   313→        self,
   314→        hidden_input_dim: int = 256,
   315→        final_target_dim: int = 4096,
   316→        num_splits=4,
   317→        reduce_factor=2,
   318→    ):
   319→        super().__init__()
   320→
   321→        self.hidden_input_dim = hidden_input_dim
   322→        self.final_target_dim = final_target_dim
   323→        self.num_splits = num_splits
   324→        self.reduce_factor = reduce_factor
   325→
   326→        final_output_size = self.final_target_dim
   327→
   328→        # Creates an array where we end with final_size and have num_splits + 1
   329→        # different entries in it (e.g., num_splits = 1 with final dim 4096 has
   330→        # [2048, 4096])
   331→        layer_dims = [
   332→            int(np.ceil(final_output_size / (reduce_factor**num_split)))
   333→            for num_split in range(num_splits + 1)
   334→        ][::-1]
   335→
   336→        # Start by predicting into the very first layer dim (e.g., 256  -> 256)
   337→        self.output_dims = layer_dims
   338→
   339→        # Define initial predict module
   340→        self.initial_predict = nn.Sequential(
   341→            nn.Linear(
   342→                hidden_input_dim,
   343→                layer_dims[0],
   344→            ),
   345→            nn.Sigmoid(),
   346→        )
   347→        predict_bricks = []
   348→        gate_bricks = []
   349→        for layer_dim_ind, layer_dim in enumerate(layer_dims[:-1]):
   350→            out_dim = layer_dims[layer_dim_ind + 1]
   351→
   352→            # Need to update nn.Linear layer to be fixed if the right param is
   353→            # called
   354→            lin_predict = nn.Linear(layer_dim, out_dim)
   355→            predict_brick = nn.Sequential(lin_predict, nn.Sigmoid())
   356→
   357→            gate_bricks.append(
   358→                nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(hidden_input_dim, out_dim), nn.Sigmoid())
   359→            )
   360→            predict_bricks.append(predict_brick)
   361→
   362→        self.predict_bricks = nn.ModuleList(predict_bricks)
   363→        self.gate_bricks = nn.ModuleList(gate_bricks)
   364→
   365→    def forward(self, hidden):
   366→        """forward.
   367→
   368→        Return dict mapping output dim to the
   369→
   370→        """
   371→        cur_pred = self.initial_predict(hidden)
   372→        output_preds = [cur_pred]
   373→        for _out_dim, predict_brick, gate_brick in zip(
   374→            self.output_dims[1:], self.predict_bricks, self.gate_bricks
   375→        ):
   376→            gate_outs = gate_brick(hidden)
   377→            pred_out = predict_brick(cur_pred)
   378→            cur_pred = gate_outs * pred_out
   379→            output_preds.append(cur_pred)
   380→        return output_preds
   381→
   382→
   383→def _get_clones(module, N):
   384→    return nn.ModuleList([copy.deepcopy(module) for i in range(N)])
   385→

    12→from torch.linalg import LinAlgError
    13→from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
    14→from tqdm import tqdm

    16→import annotix_ml.distributed as dist
    17→from annotix_ml.distributed.pipeline_parallelism import save_checkpoint
    18→from annotix_ml.graphtransf.arch.digress_meta_arch import DigressMetaArch
    19→from annotix_ml.graphtransf.data.datacollator import collateGraph, collateGraphStatic
    20→from annotix_ml.graphtransf.data.data_utils import (
    21→    batch_graph_to_smiles,
    22→    batch_graph_to_smiles_digress,
    23→)
    24→from annotix_ml.graphtransf.data.atoms_data import TYPE_EDGES
    25→from annotix_ml.graphtransf.data.loaders import make_datasets
    26→from annotix_ml.graphtransf.data.samplers import InfiniteSampler
    27→from annotix_ml.graphtransf.math.metrics import (

    31→from annotix_ml.graphtransf.train.setup import setup
