    35→def get_args():
    36→    parser = ArgumentParser()
    37→    parser.add_argument("--config", type=str, required=True)
    38→    parser.add_argument("--project-name", type=str, required=False)
    39→    parser.add_argument("--save-path", type=str, required=False)
    40→    parser.add_argument("--extra-features", type=str, required=False)
    41→    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, required=False)
    42→    parser.add_argument("--num-train-steps", type=int, required=False)
    43→    parser.add_argument("--num-diffusion-steps", type=int, required=False)
    44→    parser.add_argument("--distributed-strat", type=str, required=False)
    45→
    46→    return parser.parse_args()
    47→
    48→
    49→def do_eval(
    50→    model: DigressMetaArch,
    51→    eval_loader: DataLoader,
    52→    device: torch.device,
    53→    expected_bs: int | None = None,
    54→) -> dict[str, float]:
    55→    DisableLog("rdApp.*")
    56→    metrics = defaultdict(list)
    57→    for batch in tqdm(
    58→        eval_loader, desc="evaluation", disable=not dist.is_main_process()
    59→    ):
    60→        # Move the elements to the device of interest
    61→        batch = [v.to(device) if isinstance(v, torch.Tensor) else v for v in batch]
    62→
    63→        # Unpack the elements
    64→        nodes, edges, mask = batch
    65→
    66→        # If last batch, then size will be < to the one planned by schedule
    67→        # To avoid error -> skip it when there is a schedule (ie pp)
    68→        if model.eval_schedule:
    69→            if nodes.shape[0] != expected_bs:
    70→                continue
    71→
    72→        # Noise the elements
    73→        nodes_noised, edges_noised, sampled_t = model.noiser(nodes, edges, mask)
    74→
    75→        # Compute the predictions
    76→        try:
    77→            pN, pE = model.forward(
    78→                nodes_noised, edges_noised, mask, sampled_t
    79→            )  # (bs, n, n_atoms), (bs, n, n, n_edges)
    80→        except LinAlgError:
    81→            continue
    82→
    83→        # Non-last ranks in pipeline parallelism get None outputs;
    84→        # they must keep looping so every rank calls schedule.step().
    85→        if pN is None or pE is None:
    86→            continue
    87→
    88→        # Make the prediction graph
    89→        N_ = torch.nn.functional.one_hot(
    90→            pN.argmax(-1), num_classes=pN.shape[-1]
    91→        )  # (bs, n, n_atoms)
    92→        E_ = torch.nn.functional.one_hot(
    93→            pE.argmax(-1), num_classes=pE.shape[-1]
    94→        )  # (bs, n, n, n_edges)
    95→
    96→        # Convert the graph to smiles
    97→        true_smiles = batch_graph_to_smiles(
    98→            nodes, edges, mask, model.valid_elements
    99→        )  # (bs,)
   100→        pred_smiles = batch_graph_to_smiles(N_, E_, mask, model.valid_elements)  # (bs,)
   101→
   102→        # Compute the metrics
   103→        batch_metrics = compute_metrics(
   104→            pred_smiles,
   105→            true_smiles,
   106→            pN,
   107→            pE,
   108→            nodes,
   109→            edges,
   110→            mask,
   111→        )
   112→
   113→        # Compute accuracy per node type
   114→        target_nodes = nodes.argmax(-1)
   115→        pred_nodes = pN.argmax(-1)
   116→        valid_mask = mask.bool()
   117→
   118→        target_nodes_flat = target_nodes[valid_mask]
   119→        pred_nodes_flat = pred_nodes[valid_mask]
   120→
   121→        for i, atom_type in enumerate(model.valid_elements):
   122→            atom_mask = target_nodes_flat == i
   123→            if atom_mask.sum() > 0:
   124→                acc = (pred_nodes_flat[atom_mask] == i).float().mean().item()
   125→                batch_metrics[f"accuracy_node_{atom_type}"] = [acc]
   126→
   127→        # Compute accuracy per edge type
   128→        target_edges = edges.argmax(-1)
   129→        pred_edges = pE.argmax(-1)
   130→        edge_mask = mask.unsqueeze(2) * mask.unsqueeze(1)
   131→        edge_mask = edge_mask.bool()
   132→
   133→        target_edges_flat = target_edges[edge_mask]
   134→        pred_edges_flat = pred_edges[edge_mask]
   135→
   136→        if len(target_edges_flat) > 0:
   137→            acc_edge = (pred_edges_flat == target_edges_flat).float().mean().item()
   138→            batch_metrics["accuracy_edge_global"] = [acc_edge]
   139→
   140→        for i, edge_type in enumerate(TYPE_EDGES):
   141→            edge_type_mask = target_edges_flat == i
   142→            if edge_type_mask.sum() > 0:
   143→                acc = (pred_edges_flat[edge_type_mask] == i).float().mean().item()
   144→                batch_metrics[f"accuracy_edge_{str(edge_type)}"] = [acc]
   145→
   146→        # Accumulate metrics
   147→        for k, v in batch_metrics.items():
   148→            metrics[k].extend(v)
   149→
   150→    # Average and print metrics
   151→    final_metrics = {}
   152→    for k, v in metrics.items():
   153→        if len(v) > 0:
   154→            final_metrics[k] = sum(v) / len(v)
   155→        else:
   156→            final_metrics[k] = 0.0
   157→
   158→    return final_metrics
   159→
   160→
   161→def generate_samples(
   162→    model: DigressMetaArch,
   163→    num_samples: int,
   164→    num_nodes_dist: torch.Tensor,
   165→    batch_size: int,
   166→) -> tuple[float, float, list[str]]:
   167→    # Generate the graphs
   168→    print(f"Generating {num_samples} graphs in batches of {batch_size}...")
   169→    all_gen_smiles = []
   170→    all_gen_smiles_digress = []
   171→    samples_generated = 0
   172→
   173→    while samples_generated < num_samples:
   174→        # Sample from the distribution
   175→        n = (
   176→            num_nodes_dist.unsqueeze(0)
   177→            .expand((batch_size, -1))
   178→            .multinomial(1)
   179→            .squeeze(-1)
   180→            + 1
   181→        )
   182→
   183→        try:
   184→            gen_N, gen_E, gen_mask = model.generate(
   185→                num_samples=n, max_nodes=n.max(), progress_bar=True
   186→            )
   187→
   188→            # Convert to smiles
   189→            gen_smiles = batch_graph_to_smiles(
   190→                gen_N, gen_E, gen_mask, model.valid_elements
   191→            )
   192→            all_gen_smiles.extend(gen_smiles)
   193→
   194→            # Convert to smiles with Digress method
   195→            gen_smiles_digress = batch_graph_to_smiles_digress(
   196→                gen_N, gen_E, gen_mask, model.valid_elements
   197→            )
   198→            all_gen_smiles_digress.extend(gen_smiles_digress)
   199→
   200→        except LinAlgError:
   201→            print("LinAlgError during generation batch, skipping batch...")
   202→            continue
   203→
   204→        samples_generated += batch_size
   205→
   206→    # Trim to exactly num_samples to avoid overshoot bias in validity metrics.
   207→    all_gen_smiles = all_gen_smiles[:num_samples]
   208→    all_gen_smiles_digress = all_gen_smiles_digress[:num_samples]
   209→
   210→    valid_smiles = [s for s in all_gen_smiles if s]
   211→    valid_smiles_digress = [s for s in all_gen_smiles_digress if s]
   212→
   213→    # Compute the validity
   214→    validity = len(valid_smiles) / len(all_gen_smiles) if all_gen_smiles else 0
   215→    validity_digress = (
   216→        len(valid_smiles_digress) / len(all_gen_smiles_digress)
   217→        if all_gen_smiles_digress
   218→        else 0
   219→    )
   220→
   221→    return validity, validity_digress, valid_smiles
   222→
   223→
   224→def train(cfg):
   225→    # Select the device for the training
   226→    device = (
   227→        torch.device("cuda")
   228→        if torch.cuda.is_available()
   229→        else torch.device("mps")
   230→        if torch.mps.is_available()
   231→        else torch.device("cpu")
   232→    )
   233→    print(f"Using device: {device}\n")
   234→
   235→    # Main rank builds or loads the cache first
   236→    train_dataset, valid_dataset = make_datasets(
   237→        cfg.dataset.data_path,
   238→        cfg.dataset.smile_column,
   239→        cfg.dataset.split_column,
   240→        cfg.dataset.val_tag,
   241→        verbose=True,
   242→        cache_path=cfg.dataset.get("cache_path"),
   243→        save_cache=dist.is_main_process(),
   244→    )
   245→
   246→    # Determine the collation function and distributed data rank/size
   247→    data_rank = dist.get_global_rank()
   248→    data_size = dist.get_global_size()
   249→
   250→    if cfg.train.get("distributed") == "pipeline":
   251→        # In Pipeline Parallelism, all ranks in the same pipeline
   252→        # (which is the whole world here) must see the same data.
   253→        data_rank = 0
   254→        data_size = 1
   255→        print(
   256→            f"Pipeline Parallelism detected: setting data_rank={data_rank}, data_size={data_size} to synchronize input/targets"
   257→        )
   258→        # Derive n_max from the distribution of number of atoms
   259→        n_max = len(train_dataset.num_atoms_dist)
   260→        collate_fn = partial(collateGraphStatic, n_max=n_max)
   261→        print(f"Using static shape data collator with n_max={n_max}")
   262→
   263→    else:
   264→        collate_fn = collateGraph
   265→
   266→    # Prepare the save path & check if there is already some existing checkpoints
   267→    save_path = cfg.train.save_path
   268→    last_epoch = 0
   269→    checkpoint_path = None
   270→
   271→    if not os.path.isdir(save_path):
   272→        if dist.is_main_process():
   273→            os.makedirs(save_path)
   274→            # Save a copy of the config file
   275→            OmegaConf.save(config=cfg, f=os.path.join(save_path, "config.yaml"))
   276→
   277→    if dist.is_enabled():
   278→        torch.distributed.barrier()
   279→
   280→    # Check if there are already model weights in the saving path
   281→    model_checkpoints = [f for f in os.listdir(save_path) if f.endswith(".pt")]
   282→    if len(model_checkpoints) > 0:
   283→        last_checkpoint = sorted(model_checkpoints, key=lambda y: int(y.split(".")[0]))[
   284→            -1
   285→        ]
   286→        checkpoint_path = os.path.join(save_path, last_checkpoint)
   287→        last_epoch = int(last_checkpoint.split(".")[0])
   288→
   289→        print(f"Checkpoints found, loading from the weights at {checkpoint_path}.")
   290→        digress = DigressMetaArch.load_pretrained(
   291→            cfg,
   292→            device,
   293→            checkpoint_path,
   294→            train_dataset.valid_elements,
   295→            train_dataset.nodes_distribution,
   296→            train_dataset.edges_distribution,
   297→            train_dataset.max_weight,
   298→        )
   299→
   300→    else:
   301→        # Define the model
   302→        print("No checkpoints found, init from zero.")
   303→        digress = DigressMetaArch.init_from_cfg(
   304→            cfg,
   305→            device,
   306→            train_dataset.valid_elements,
   307→            train_dataset.nodes_distribution,
   308→            train_dataset.edges_distribution,
   309→            max_weight=train_dataset.max_weight,
   310→        )
   311→
   312→    if dist.is_main_process():
   313→        print(f"Logging with main rank as : {dist._MAIN_RANK}")
   314→
   315→        wandb_id_file = os.path.join(save_path, "wandb_run_id.txt")
   316→        if last_epoch > 0 and os.path.isfile(wandb_id_file):
   317→            with open(wandb_id_file) as f:
   318→                wandb_run_id = f.read().strip()
   319→            wandb.init(
   320→                project=cfg.run.project,
   321→                name=cfg.run.name,
   322→                config=OmegaConf.to_container(cfg, resolve=True),
   323→                id=wandb_run_id,
   324→                resume="allow",
   325→            )
   326→        else:
   327→            wandb.init(
   328→                project=cfg.run.project,
   329→                name=cfg.run.name,
   330→                config=OmegaConf.to_container(cfg, resolve=True),
   331→            )
   332→            with open(wandb_id_file, "w") as f:
   333→                f.write(wandb.run.id)
   334→
   335→    # Make the DataLoaders
   336→    sample_count = len(train_dataset)
   337→    shuffle = True
   338→    seed = cfg.train.seed
   339→    advance = (
   340→        ((last_epoch + 1) * cfg.train.batch_size) % len(train_dataset)
   341→        if (last_epoch > 0 and not shuffle)
   342→        else 0
   343→    )

    90→        # Instanciate the diffusion model
    91→        self.valid_elements = valid_elements
    92→        self.natoms = len(valid_elements)
    93→        self.nbonds = len(TYPE_EDGES)
    94→
    95→        if no_y:
    96→            self.diffuser = GnnNodeEdgesWithoutY(
    97→                d=d,
    98→                de=de,
    99→                n_heads=n_heads,
   100→                node_features=self.node_features,
   101→                global_features=self.global_features,
   102→                n_layers=n_layers,
   103→                natoms=self.natoms,
   104→                nbonds=self.nbonds,
   105→            ).to(device)
   106→
   107→        else:
   108→            self.diffuser = GnnNodeEdges(
   109→                d=d,
   110→                de=de,
   111→                dy=dy,
   112→                n_heads=n_heads,
   113→                y_update=y_update,
   114→                node_features=self.node_features,
   115→                global_features=self.global_features,
   116→                n_layers=n_layers,
   117→                natoms=self.natoms,
   118→                nbonds=self.nbonds,
   119→            ).to(device)
   120→
   121→        self.no_y = no_y
   122→
   123→        # Instanciate the noising model
   124→        if noise_strategy == "uniform":
   125→            nodes_distribution = torch.ones(self.natoms) / self.natoms
   126→            edges_distribution = torch.ones(len(TYPE_EDGES)) / len(TYPE_EDGES)
   127→
   128→        elif noise_strategy == "distribution":
   129→            pass
   130→
   131→        else:
   132→            raise ValueError(f"{noise_strategy} is not a recognized noise strategy.")
   133→
   134→        if (nodes_distribution is None) | (edges_distribution is None):
   135→            raise TypeError("edges or nodes distribution not given.")
   136→
   137→        self.nodes_distribution = nodes_distribution
   138→        self.edges_distribution = edges_distribution
   139→
   140→        self.noiser = NoisingModel(
   141→            diffusion_steps=diffusion_steps,
   142→            nodes_distribution=nodes_distribution,
   143→            edges_distribution=edges_distribution,
   144→        )
   145→        self.noiser.move_to(device)
   146→
   147→        # Put some variables in case of distributed training
   148→        self.rank = -1
   149→        self.train_schedule = None
   150→        self.eval_schedule = None
   151→        self.train_model = None
   152→        self.eval_model = None

   154→    @classmethod

   203→    @classmethod
   204→    def load_pretrained(
   205→        cls,
   206→        cfg: DictConfig,
   207→        device: torch.device,
   208→        model_path: str,
   209→        valid_elements: list[str] | None,
   210→        nodes_distribution: torch.Tensor | None,
   211→        edges_distribution: torch.Tensor | None,
   212→        max_weight: float | None = None,
   213→    ):
   214→        """
   215→        Load a pretrained DigressMetaArch model from a file.
   216→        Note that only the weights for the diffuser model are loaded from the specified file.
   217→
   218→        Args:
   219→            cfg (DictConfig): Configuration object. Refer to `configs/default_config.yaml`
   220→                for the necessary configuration keys.
   221→            device (torch.device): Device on which the model should be loaded.
   222→            model_path (str): Path to the saved weights file (containing the diffuser state_dict).
   223→            valid_elements (list[str] | None): List of valid atomic element symbols.
   224→            nodes_distribution (torch.Tensor | None): Marginal distribution of node types.
   225→            edges_distribution (torch.Tensor | None): Marginal distribution of edge types.
   226→            max_weight (float | None, optional): Maximum molecular weight for normalization. Defaults to None.
   227→
   228→        Returns:
   229→            DigressMetaArch: Loaded model instance.
   230→        """
   231→        if not os.path.exists(model_path):
   232→            raise ValueError(f"{model_path} is not an existing path.")
   233→
   234→        model = cls.init_from_cfg(
   235→            cfg,
   236→            device,
   237→            valid_elements,
   238→            nodes_distribution,
   239→            edges_distribution,
   240→            max_weight,
   241→        )
   242→
   243→        saved = torch.load(model_path, weights_only=True)
   244→        # Support both the old format (bare state_dict) and the new format
   245→        # ({"model": state_dict, "optimizer": ...}).
   246→        if isinstance(saved, dict) and "model" in saved:
   247→            saved_model = saved["model"]
   248→        else:
   249→            saved_model = saved
   250→        model.diffuser.load_state_dict(saved_model)
   251→
   252→        return model

   254→    @property
   255→    def global_features(self) -> int:
   256→        # noising step is always a parameter
   257→        global_features = 1
   258→        for name in self.extra_features:
   259→            if name == "laplacian_embedding":
   260→                global_features += (
   261→                    self.num_ev + 1
   262→                )  # eigvalues + num_connected_components
   263→
   264→            elif name == "node_cycle":
   265→                global_features += 4
   266→
   267→            elif name == "valence_features":
   268→                global_features += 1
   269→
   270→        return global_features

   275→        for name in self.extra_features:
   276→            if name == "laplacian_embedding":
   277→                node_features += self.num_ev + 1  # eigvalues + num_connected_components
   278→
   279→            elif name == "node_cycle":

   281→
   282→            elif name == "valence_features":

   287→    def compute_extra_features(
   288→        self,
   289→        nodes: torch.Tensor,
   290→        edges: torch.Tensor,
   291→        mask: torch.Tensor,
   292→        t: torch.Tensor,
   293→        **kwargs,
   294→    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
   295→        """
   296→        Compute extra node and global features for the current graph state.
   297→
   298→        Args:
   299→            nodes (torch.Tensor): Node features tensor of shape (bs, n, natoms).
   300→            edges (torch.Tensor): Edge features tensor of shape (bs, n, n, nedges).
   301→            mask (torch.Tensor): Mask tensor of shape (bs, n).
   302→            t (torch.Tensor): Timestep tensor of shape (bs, 1).
   303→            **kwargs: Extra arguments for subclasses (e.g. spectral features).
   304→
   305→        Returns:
   306→            tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: A tuple containing:
   307→                - node_features (torch.Tensor): Computed node features of shape (bs, n, node_features).
   308→                - global_features (torch.Tensor): Computed global features of shape (bs, global_features).
   309→        """
   310→        # Init the list of node and global_features
   311→        node_features_list = []
   312→        global_features_list = []
   313→
   314→        for name in self.extra_features:
   315→            if name == "laplacian_embedding":
   316→                if self.num_ev is None:
   317→                    raise ValueError("k must be specified for laplacian_embedding.")
   318→
   319→                node_features, global_features = laplacian_embedding(
   320→                    edges, self.num_ev, mask
   321→                )
   322→
   323→            elif name == "node_cycle":
   324→                node_features, global_features = node_cycle(edges, mask)
   325→
   326→            elif name == "valence_features":
   327→                node_features_val = valency(edges, mask)
   328→
   329→                node_features_charge = charge(nodes, edges, mask, self.valid_elements)
   330→
   331→                global_features_weight = weight(
   332→                    nodes,
   333→                    self.valid_elements,
   334→                    self.max_weight,
   335→                )
   336→
   337→                node_features = torch.cat(
   338→                    [node_features_val, node_features_charge], dim=-1
   339→                )
   340→                global_features = global_features_weight
   341→
   342→            else:
   343→                raise ValueError(f"{name} is not a recognized extra feature.")
   344→
   345→            # Unpack for cases with global and local outputs
   346→            if node_features is not None:
   347→                node_features_list.append(node_features)
   348→
   349→            if global_features is not None:
   350→                global_features_list.append(global_features)
   351→
   352→            global_features = None
   353→            node_features = None
   354→
   355→        if node_features_list:
   356→            pos_emb = torch.cat(node_features_list, dim=-1)  # (bs, n, n_features)
   357→        else:
   358→            pos_emb = torch.zeros((*nodes.shape[:-1], 0), device=nodes.device)
   359→
   360→        if global_features_list:
   361→            y = torch.cat(global_features_list, dim=-1)  # (bs, n_global_features)
   362→        else:
   363→            y = torch.zeros((nodes.shape[0], 0), device=nodes.device)
   364→
   365→        # Add the noising step to y
   366→        t = t.to(device=y.device, dtype=y.dtype) / self.noiser.T
   367→        y = torch.cat([y, t], dim=-1)
   368→
   369→        return pos_emb, y
   370→
   371→    def forward(
   372→        self,
   373→        nodes: torch.Tensor,
   374→        edges: torch.Tensor,
   375→        mask: torch.Tensor,
   376→        t: torch.Tensor | None = None,
   377→        **kwargs,
   378→    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
   379→        """
   380→        Run the forward pass: noise the input batch, then predict the clean graph.
   381→        This method first adds noise to the input nodes and edges using `self.noiser`,
   382→        and then uses `self.diffuser` to predict the clean graph probabilities.
   383→
   384→        Args:
   385→            nodes (torch.Tensor): Node features of shape (bs, n, natoms).
   386→            edges (torch.Tensor): Edge features of shape (bs, n, n, nedges).
   387→            mask (torch.Tensor): Mask tensor of shape (bs, n).
   388→            t (torch.Tensor | None): Optional timestep tensor.
   389→            **kwargs: Extra arguments passed to compute_extra_features.
   390→
   391→        Returns:
   392→            tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: A tuple containing:
   393→                - pN (torch.Tensor): Predicted node probabilities of shape (bs, n, natoms).
   394→                - pE (torch.Tensor): Predicted edge probabilities of shape (bs, n, n, nedges).
   395→        """
   396→        # Use the schedule to make the forward pass if pp distributed
   397→        if self.eval_schedule:
   398→            if self.eval_model.is_first:
   399→                # Only the first stage needs the extra features; non-first stages
   400→                # receive intermediate activations from the previous stage via P2P.
   401→                pos_emb, y = self.compute_extra_features(
   402→                    nodes, edges, mask, t, **kwargs
   403→                )  # (bs, node_features), (bs, global_features)
   404→                input_args = (edges, mask, y, pos_emb, nodes)
   405→                out = self.eval_schedule.step(*input_args)
   406→
   407→            elif self.eval_model.is_last:
   408→                out = self.eval_schedule.step()
   409→                pN, pE, *_ = out
   410→
   411→            else:
   412→                out = self.eval_schedule.step()
   413→
   414→        # For data parallelism (DDP), forward() is only called under torch.no_grad()
   415→        # during eval/generation, so calling self.diffuser directly is correct —
   416→        # no gradient sync is needed.
   417→        else:
   418→            pos_emb, y = self.compute_extra_features(
   419→                nodes, edges, mask, t, **kwargs
   420→            )  # (bs, node_features), (bs, global_features)
   421→            out = self.diffuser(edges, mask, y, pos_emb, nodes)
   422→            pN, pE, *_ = out
   423→
   424→        if out is None:
   425→            pN, pE = None, None
   426→
   427→        return pN, pE
   428→
   429→    def forward_backward(
   430→        self,
   431→        nodes: torch.Tensor,
   432→        edges: torch.Tensor,
   433→        mask: torch.Tensor,
   434→        **kwargs,
   435→    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
   436→        """
   437→        Run the forward pass: noise the input batch, then predict the clean graph.
   438→        This method first adds noise to the input nodes and edges using `self.noiser`,
   439→        and then uses `self.diffuser` to predict the clean graph probabilities.
   440→
   441→        Args:
   442→            nodes (torch.Tensor): Node features of shape (bs, n, natoms).
   443→            edges (torch.Tensor): Edge features of shape (bs, n, n, nedges).
   444→            mask (torch.Tensor): Mask tensor of shape (bs, n).
   445→            **kwargs: Extra arguments passed to compute_extra_features.
   446→
   447→        Returns:
   448→            tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: A tuple containing:
   449→                - pN (torch.Tensor): Predicted node probabilities of shape (bs, n, natoms).
   450→                - pE (torch.Tensor): Predicted edge probabilities of shape (bs, n, n, nedges).
   451→        """
   452→        # Compute the output of the diffuser
   453→        if self.train_schedule:
   454→            # Make the target -> need to stack to be splitted for mb
   455→            target = torch.hstack(
   456→                [nodes.flatten(start_dim=1), edges.flatten(start_dim=1)]
   457→            )  # (bs, n * natoms + n * n * nedges)
   458→
   459→            if self.train_model.is_first:
   460→                # Only the first stage needs noised inputs and extra features;
   461→                # non-first stages receive intermediate activations via P2P.
   462→                N_noised, E_noised, sampled_t = self.noiser(nodes, edges, mask)
   463→                pos_emb, y = self.compute_extra_features(
   464→                    N_noised, E_noised, mask, sampled_t, **kwargs
   465→                )  # (bs, node_features), (bs, global_features)
   466→                input_args = (E_noised, mask, y, pos_emb, N_noised)
   467→                out = self.train_schedule.step(*input_args)
   468→
   469→            elif self.train_model.is_last:
   470→                losses = []
   471→                out = self.train_schedule.step(target=target, losses=losses)
   472→                loss = sum(losses) / len(losses)
   473→                pN, pE, *_ = out
   474→
   475→            else:
   476→                out = self.train_schedule.step()
   477→
   478→        elif self.train_model is not None:
   479→            # Data parallelism: call through the DDP wrapper so that loss.backward()
   480→            # triggers the all-reduce gradient synchronisation across ranks.
   481→            N_noised, E_noised, sampled_t = self.noiser(nodes, edges, mask)
   482→            pos_emb, y = self.compute_extra_features(
   483→                N_noised, E_noised, mask, sampled_t, **kwargs
   484→            )  # (bs, node_features), (bs, global_features)
   485→            out = self.train_model(E_noised, mask, y, pos_emb, N_noised)
   486→            pN, pE, *_ = out
   487→            loss = digress_loss(pN, pE, nodes, edges, mask, self.loss_ratio)
   488→            loss.backward()
   489→
   490→        else:
   491→            # No distributed training
   492→            N_noised, E_noised, sampled_t = self.noiser(nodes, edges, mask)
   493→            pos_emb, y = self.compute_extra_features(
   494→                N_noised, E_noised, mask, sampled_t, **kwargs
   495→            )  # (bs, node_features), (bs, global_features)
   496→            input_args = (E_noised, mask, y, pos_emb, N_noised)
   497→            out = self.diffuser(*input_args)
   498→            pN, pE, *_ = out
   499→            loss = digress_loss(pN, pE, nodes, edges, mask, self.loss_ratio)
   500→            loss.backward()
   501→
   502→        if out is None:
   503→            pN, pE, loss = None, None, None
   504→
   505→        return pN, pE, loss
   506→
   507→    @torch.no_grad()
   508→    def generate(
   509→        self,
   510→        num_samples: int | torch.Tensor,
   511→        max_nodes: int,
   512→        min_nodes: int = 1,
   513→        progress_bar=False,
   514→        num_attempts: int = 3,
   515→        **kwargs,
   516→    ):
   517→        """
   518→        Generate new graphs using the reverse diffusion process.
   519→
   520→        The generation starts from pure noise (sampled according to the marginal distributions)
   521→        and iteratively applies the reverse diffusion step. At each step `t`, the model
   522→        predicts the clean graph, and the sample for `t-1` is drawn from the posterior
   523→        distribution `q(z_{t-1} | z_t, z_0)`.
   524→
   525→        Args:
   526→            num_samples (int | torch.Tensor):
   527→                - If int: Number of samples to generate. The size (node count) of each
   528→                  generated graph is randomly sampled between `min_nodes` and `max_nodes`.
   529→                - If torch.Tensor: A 1D tensor of shape (num_samples,) where each element
   530→                  specifies the exact number of nodes for a sample. The total number of
   531→                  samples is then determined by the length of this tensor.
   532→            max_nodes (int): Maximum number of nodes for the generated graphs.
   533→            min_nodes (int, optional): Minimum number of nodes for the generated graphs. Defaults to 1.
   534→            progress_bar (bool, optional): Whether to show a progress bar during denoising. Defaults to False.
   535→            num_attempts (int, optional): Number of attempts to generate graphs (to handle potential LinAlgError). Defaults to 3.
   536→            **kwargs: Extra arguments passed to compute_extra_features (e.g. conditioning spectra).
   537→
   538→        Raises:
   539→            LinAlgError: If generation fails after all attempts due to numerical instability.
   540→
   541→        Returns:
   542→            tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: A tuple containing:
   543→                - N (torch.Tensor): Generated node features of shape (bs, n, natoms).
   544→                - E (torch.Tensor): Generated edge features of shape (bs, n, n, nedges).
   545→                - mask (torch.Tensor): Generated masks of shape (bs, n).
   546→        """
   547→        # Preserve the original tensor so retry iterations don't see mutated int.
   548→        if isinstance(num_samples, torch.Tensor):
   549→            assert len(num_samples.shape) == 1, (
   550→                f"Wrong shape for num_samples: {num_samples.shape}"
   551→            )
   552→            n_sizes = num_samples
   553→            num_samples = n_sizes.shape[0]
   554→        else:
   555→            n_sizes = None
   556→
   557→        i = 0
   558→        while i < num_attempts:
   559→            # sample random n
   560→            if n_sizes is not None:
   561→                n = n_sizes
   562→            else:
   563→                n = torch.randint(min_nodes, max_nodes, (num_samples,))
   564→
   565→            # Make the mask
   566→            mask = torch.stack(
   567→                [
   568→                    torch.cat([torch.ones(int(m)), torch.zeros(max_nodes - int(m))])
   569→                    for m in n
   570→                ]
   571→            )  # (bs, max_nodes)
   572→            mask = mask.to(self.device)
   573→
   574→            # Make the distributions based on the dataset
   575→            N_dist = (
   576→                self.nodes_distribution.unsqueeze(0)
   577→                .unsqueeze(0)
   578→                .expand(num_samples, max_nodes, -1)
   579→            )  # (bs, n, n_atoms)
   580→            E_dist = (
   581→                self.edges_distribution.unsqueeze(0)
   582→                .unsqueeze(0)
   583→                .unsqueeze(0)
   584→                .expand(num_samples, max_nodes, max_nodes, -1)
   585→            )  # (bs, n, n, n_edges)
   586→
   587→            # sample a random graph
   588→            N, E = sample_discrete_features(
   589→                N_dist, E_dist, mask
   590→            )  # (bs, n, n_atoms), (bs, n, n, n_edges)
   591→
   592→            # NCCL requires all broadcast tensors to be on a CUDA device; move
   593→            # N and E to device before the collective calls.
   594→            N = N.float().to(self.device)
   595→            E = E.float().to(self.device)
   596→
   597→            # Denoise the graph
   598→            self.diffuser.eval()
   599→
   600→            if progress_bar:
   601→                t_range = tqdm(
   602→                    reversed(range(1, self.noiser.T)),
   603→                    total=self.noiser.T - 1,
   604→                    desc="Denoising",
   605→                    disable=not is_main_process(),
   606→                )
   607→            else:
   608→                t_range = reversed(range(1, self.noiser.T))
   609→
   610→            try:
   611→                for t in t_range:
   612→                    # Convert to float for compatibility with noising model
   613→                    N = N.float().to(self.device)
   614→                    E = E.float().to(self.device)
   615→
   616→                    # Mask the graph
   617→                    N = mask_any_tensor(N, mask, fill=0)  # (bs, n, n_atoms)
   618→                    E = mask_any_tensor(E, mask, fill=0)  # (bs, n, n, n_edges)
   619→
   620→                    # Make the tensor for timestep
   621→                    t_tensor = (
   622→                        torch.tensor(t).unsqueeze(-1).expand((num_samples, -1))
   623→                    )  # bs, 1
   624→
   625→                    # Forward pass — all ranks must call this to drive th   e pipeline.
   626→                    pN, pE = self.forward(N, E, mask, t_tensor, **kwargs)
   627→
   628→                    # Only the last pipeline rank gets valid predictions.
   629→                    if pN is not None and pE is not None:
   630→                        pN = pN.softmax(-1)  #  (bs, n, n_atoms)
   631→                        pE = pE.softmax(-1)  #  (bs, n, n, n_edges)
   632→
   633→                        # Compute the posterior distribution
   634→                        post_N, post_E = self.noiser.get_posterior(
   635→                            N, E, t
   636→                        )  # (bs, n, n_atoms, n_atoms), (bs, n, n, n_edges, n_edges)
   637→
   638→                        # Compute the combined distribution -> element-wise multiplication
   639→                        # Then sum over all the possible starting values (dim -2)
   640→                        probN = (post_N * pN.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(
   641→                            dim=-2
   642→                        )  # (bs, n, n_atoms)
   643→                        probE = (post_E * pE.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(
   644→                            dim=-2
   645→                        )  # (bs, n, n, n_edges)
   646→
   647→                        # Normalize with epsilon to prevent division by zero
   648→                        eps = 1e-6
   649→                        probN = probN / (
   650→                            probN.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + eps
   651→                        )  # (bs, n, n_atoms)
   652→                        probE = probE / (
   653→                            probE.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + eps
   654→                        )  # (bs, n, n, n_edges)
   655→
   656→                        # Sample from the combined distribution
   657→                        N, E = sample_discrete_features(
   658→                            probN, probE, mask
   659→                        )  # (bs, n, n_atoms), (bs, n, n, n_edges)
   660→
   661→                return N, E, mask
   662→
   663→            except LinAlgError as e:
   664→                print(
   665→                    f"Generation failed, attempt {i + 1} / {num_attempts}: "
   666→                    f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
   667→                )
   668→                i += 1
   669→
   670→    # TODO: error when valid bs != train bs -> put an example_batch for eval_model would fix that but make code longer.
   671→    def _setup_distributed(
   672→        self, mode: Literal["pipeline", "tensor"], num_microbatches: int, example_batch
   673→    ):
   674→        self.rank = get_global_rank()
   675→        if mode == "pipeline":
   676→            # Slice the example batch to the micro-batch size
   677→            N, E, mask = example_batch
   678→            bs = N.shape[0]
   679→            mb_size = bs // num_microbatches
   680→
   681→            # Make the example microbatch for the pipeline
   682→            N_mb = N[:mb_size]
   683→            E_mb = E[:mb_size]
   684→            mask_mb = mask[:mb_size]
   685→
   686→            # Compute the extra features for the example microbatch
   687→            t = torch.randint(
   688→                1, self.noiser.T, (mb_size,), device=self.device
   689→            ).unsqueeze(1)
   690→            pos_emb, y = self.compute_extra_features(N_mb, E_mb, mask_mb, t=t)
   691→            example_input = (E_mb, mask_mb, y, pos_emb, N_mb)
   692→
   693→            # Move the input to the correct device
   694→            example_input = tuple(v.to(self.device) for v in example_input)
   695→
   696→            # Split the model in pipeline
   697→            train_model, eval_model = auto_model_split(self.diffuser, example_input)
   698→            self.train_model = train_model
   699→            self.eval_model = eval_model
   700→
   701→            # Make a loss function for the pipeline
   702→            def loss_fn(logits: list[torch.Tensor], target: torch.Tensor):
   703→                # Unpack the predictions in normalized order (h, e, mask)
   704→                pN, pE, mask = logits
   705→
   706→                # Remake the nodes and edges
   707→                _, n, natoms = pN.shape
   708→                *_, nedges = pE.shape
   709→
   710→                nodes = target[:, : (n * natoms)].unflatten(-1, (n, natoms))
   711→                edges = target[:, (n * natoms) :].unflatten(-1, (n, n, nedges))
   712→
   713→                loss = digress_loss(pN, pE, nodes, edges, mask, self.loss_ratio)
   714→                return loss
   715→
   716→            self.train_schedule = ScheduleGPipe(
   717→                train_model, num_microbatches, loss_fn=loss_fn
   718→            )
   719→            self.eval_schedule = ScheduleGPipe(eval_model, num_microbatches)
   720→
   721→        elif mode == "data":
   722→            self.train_model = DDP(
   723→                self.diffuser,
   724→                device_ids=[get_local_rank()],
   725→            )
   726→
   727→        elif mode == "tensor":
   728→            pass
   729→
   730→        else:
   731→            raise ValueError(f"{mode} is not a recognized distributed mode.")
   732→

1→import torch
     2→import torch.nn as nn
     3→
     4→from annotix_ml.graphtransf.layers import (
     5→    AttentionLayer,
     6→    AttentionLayerWithoutY,
     7→    EmbeddingLaplacian,
     8→    EmbeddingLaplacianWithoutY,
     9→    MLPNodeEdge,
    10→    MLPNodeEdgeWithoutY,
    11→)
    12→
    13→
    14→class GnnNodeEdges(nn.Module):
    15→    """
    16→    Implementation of the GNN model as described in https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.09699.
    17→
    18→    This model processes graph-structured data (nodes and edges) along with global features,
    19→    using a series of attention layers to update the node, edge, and global representations.
    20→
    21→    Args:
    22→        d (int): Hidden dimension for node features.
    23→        de (int): Hidden dimension for edge features.
    24→        dy (int): Hidden dimension for global features.
    25→        n_heads (int): Number of attention heads in the attention layers.
    26→        node_features (int): Dimension of input extra node features.
    27→        global_features (int): Dimension of input extra global features.
    28→        n_layers (int): Number of attention layers.
    29→        natoms (int): Number of output node types (e.g., atom types).
    30→        nbonds (int): Number of output edge types (e.g., bond types).
    31→        y_update (bool, optional): Whether to update global features in the attention layers. Defaults to True.
    32→    """
    33→
    34→    def __init__(
    35→        self,
    36→        d: int,
    37→        de: int,
    38→        dy: int,
    39→        n_heads: int,
    40→        node_features: int,
    41→        global_features: int,
    42→        n_layers: int,
    43→        natoms: int,
    44→        nbonds: int,
    45→        y_update: bool = True,
    46→    ):
    47→        """
    48→        Initialize the GnnNodeEdges model.
    49→
    50→        Args:
    51→            d (int): Hidden dimension for node features.
    52→            de (int): Hidden dimension for edge features.
    53→            dy (int): Hidden dimension for global features.
    54→            n_heads (int): Number of attention heads.
    55→            node_features (int): Dimension of input extra node features.
    56→            global_features (int): Dimension of input extra global features.
    57→            n_layers (int): Number of attention layers.
    58→            natoms (int): Number of output node types.
    59→            nbonds (int): Number of output edge types.
    60→            y_update (bool, optional): Whether to update global features. Defaults to True.
    61→        """
    62→        super().__init__()
    63→        self.d = d
    64→        self.de = de
    65→        self.dy = dy
    66→        self.n_layers = n_layers
    67→
    68→        # Make the Embedding layer
    69→        self.embedding_layer = EmbeddingLaplacian(
    70→            d, de, dy, node_features, global_features, natoms, nbonds
    71→        )
    72→
    73→        # Build the attention layers
    74→        layers: list[nn.Module] = []
    75→        for _ in range(n_layers):
    76→            layers.append(AttentionLayer(d, de, dy, n_heads, y_update))
    77→
    78→        # Build the last layer
    79→        layers.append(MLPNodeEdge(d, de, natoms, nbonds))
    80→
    81→        self.layers = nn.ModuleList(layers)
    82→
    83→    def forward(
    84→        self,
    85→        e: torch.Tensor,
    86→        mask: torch.Tensor,
    87→        y: torch.Tensor,
    88→        node_features: torch.Tensor,
    89→        h: torch.Tensor,
    90→    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    91→        """
    92→        Forward pass of the GNN model.
    93→
    94→        Args:
    95→            e (torch.Tensor): Edge features of shape (bs, n, n, nedges).
    96→            mask (torch.Tensor): Mask tensor of shape (bs, n).
    97→            y (torch.Tensor): Global features of shape (bs, dy).
    98→            node_features (torch.Tensor): Extra node features of shape (bs, n, node_features).
    99→            h (torch.Tensor): Node features of shape (bs, n, natoms).
   100→
   101→        Returns:
   102→            tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
   103→                - h (torch.Tensor): Updated node features of shape (bs, n, d).
   104→                - e (torch.Tensor): Updated edge features of shape (bs, n, n, de).
   105→                - y (torch.Tensor): Updated global features of shape (bs, dy).
   106→                - mask (torch.Tensor): Mask tensor (unchanged).
   107→        """
   108→        # y is already computed/provided in this version
   109→        h, e, y, mask = self.embedding_layer(h, e, y, node_features, mask)
   110→
   111→        for layer in self.layers:
   112→            h, e, y, mask = layer(h, e, y, mask)
   113→            mask = mask.clone()
   114→
   115→        h = h + mask.sum() * 0.0
   116→        return h, e, y, mask
   117→
   118→
   119→class GnnNodeEdgesWithoutY(nn.Module):
   120→    """
   121→    Implementation of the GNN model as described in https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.09699,
   122→    without explicit global feature updates in the attention layers.
   123→
   124→    This model is similar to `GnnNodeEdges` but does not maintain or update a separate
   125→    global feature vector `y` within its attention layers. Instead, global features
   126→    are typically concatenated with node features at the beginning.
   127→
   128→    Args:

   132→        node_features (int): Dimension of input extra node features.
   133→        global_features (int): Dimension of input extra global features.
   134→        n_layers (int): Number of attention layers.
   135→        natoms (int): Number of output node types.
   136→        nbonds (int): Number of output edge types.
   137→    """

   145→        global_features: int,
   146→        n_layers: int,
   147→        natoms: int,
   148→        nbonds: int,

    88→class Mol(object):

    91→    spectra.

    94→    def __init__(
    95→        self,
    96→        mol: Chem.Mol,
    97→        smiles: Optional[str] = None,
    98→        inchikey: Optional[str] = None,
    99→        mol_formula: Optional[str] = None,
   100→    ):
   101→        """_summary_
   102→
   103→        Args:
   104→            mol (Chem.Mol): _description_
   105→            smiles (Optional[str], optional): _description_. Defaults to None.
   106→            inchikey (Optional[str], optional): _description_. Defaults to None.
   107→            mol_formula (Optional[str], optional): _description_. Defaults to None.
   108→        """
   109→        self.mol = mol
   110→
   111→        self.smiles = smiles
   112→        if self.smiles is None:
   113→            # Isomeric smiles handled in preprocessing
   114→            self.smiles = Chem.MolToSmiles(mol)
   115→
   116→        self.inchikey = inchikey
   117→        if self.inchikey is None and self.smiles != "":
   118→            self.inchikey = Chem.MolToInchiKey(mol)

   122→            self.mol_formula = uncharged_formula(self.mol, mol_type="mol")

   124→
   125→    @classmethod
   126→    def MolFromInchi(cls, inchi: str, **kwargs):
   127→        """_summary_
   128→
   129→        Args:
   130→            inchi (str): _description_
   131→
   132→        Returns:
   133→            _type_: _description_
   134→        """
   135→        mol = Chem.MolFromInchi(inchi)
   136→
   137→        # Catch exception
   138→        if mol is None:
   139→            return None
   140→
   141→        return cls(mol=mol, smiles=None, **kwargs)
   142→
   143→    @classmethod
   144→    def MolFromSmiles(cls, smiles: str, **kwargs):
   145→        """_summary_
   146→
   147→        Args:
   148→            smiles (str): _description_
   149→
   150→        Returns:
   151→            _type_: _description_
   152→        """
   153→        if not smiles or isinstance(smiles, float):
   154→            smiles = ""
   155→
   156→        mol = Chem.MolFromSmiles(smiles)
   157→        # Catch exception
   158→        if mol is None:
   159→            return None
   160→
   161→        return cls(mol=mol, smiles=smiles, **kwargs)
   162→
   163→    @classmethod
   164→    def MolFromFormula(cls, formula: str, **kwargs):
   165→        """
   166→        Create a Mol object from a chemical formula.
   167→        This creates a molecule with atoms but no bonds.
   168→
   169→        Args:
   170→            formula (str): Chemical formula (e.g., "C6H12O6")

   173→        Returns:

   176→        # Regular expression to extract element symbols and counts from the formula

   185→            # If no count is specified, default to 1

   187→
   188→            # Get atomic number for the element
   189→            atomic_num = Chem.GetPeriodicTable().GetAtomicNumber(element)

   191→            # Add the atoms to the molecule

   207→        """_summary_

   211→        """
   212→        return self.inchikey
   213→
   214→    def get_molform(self) -> str:
   215→        """_summary_

   217→        Returns:

   219→        """
   220→        return self.mol_formula
   221→
   222→    def get_num_hs(self):
   223→        """_summary_
   224→
   225→        Raises:
   226→            ValueError: _description_
   227→
   228→        Returns:
   229→            _type_: _description_
   230→        """
   231→        """get_num_hs."""
   232→        if self.num_hs is None:
   233→            num = re.findall("H([0-9]*)", self.mol_formula)
   234→            if num is None:
   235→                out_num_hs = 0
   236→            else:
   237→                if len(num) == 0:
   238→                    out_num_hs = 0
   239→                elif len(num) == 1:
   240→                    num = num[0]
   241→                    out_num_hs = 1 if num == "" else int(num)
   242→                else:
   243→                    raise ValueError()
   244→            self.num_hs = out_num_hs
   245→        else:
   246→            out_num_hs = self.num_hs
   247→
   248→        return out_num_hs
   249→
   250→    def get_mol_mass(self):
   251→        """_summary_
   252→
   253→        Returns:
   254→            _type_: _description_
   255→        """
   256→        return Descriptors.MolWt(self.mol)

   259→        """_summary_

   261→        Returns:
   262→            Chem.Mol: _description_
   263→        """

   181→        lines, lambda line: line.startswith(">") or line.startswith("#")
   182→    )

   256→def encode_no_edge(E):
   257→    assert len(E.shape) == 4
   258→    if E.shape[-1] == 0:

   260→    no_edge = torch.sum(E, dim=3) == 0
   261→    first_elt = E[:, :, :, 0]
   262→    first_elt[no_edge] = 1
   263→    E[:, :, :, 0] = first_elt
   264→    diag = (
   265→        torch.eye(E.shape[1], dtype=torch.bool).unsqueeze(0).expand(E.shape[0], -1, -1)

   267→    E[diag] = 0

   202→def generate_samples(
   203→    model: Spec2MolMetaArch,
   204→    num_samples: int,
   205→    num_nodes_dist: torch.Tensor,
   206→    batch_size: int,

   208→    print(f"Generating {num_samples} graphs in batches of {batch_size}...")
   209→    all_gen_smiles = []
   210→    all_gen_smiles_digress = []
   211→    samples_generated = 0
   212→
   213→    while samples_generated < num_samples:
   214→        n = (
   215→            num_nodes_dist.unsqueeze(0)
   216→            .expand((batch_size, -1))
   217→            .multinomial(1)
   218→            .squeeze(-1)
   219→            + 1
   220→        )
   221→
   222→        try:
   223→            gen_N, gen_E, gen_mask = model.generate(
   224→                num_samples=n, max_nodes=n.max(), progress_bar=True
   225→            )
   226→
   227→            gen_smiles = batch_graph_to_smiles(
   228→                gen_N, gen_E, gen_mask, model.valid_elements
   229→            )
   230→            all_gen_smiles.extend(gen_smiles)
   231→
   232→            gen_smiles_digress = batch_graph_to_smiles_digress(
   233→                gen_N, gen_E, gen_mask, model.valid_elements
   234→            )
   235→            all_gen_smiles_digress.extend(gen_smiles_digress)
   236→
   237→        except LinAlgError:
   238→            print("LinAlgError during generation batch, skipping batch...")
   239→            continue
   240→
   241→        samples_generated += batch_size
   242→
   243→    # Trim to exactly num_samples to avoid overshoot bias in validity metrics.
   244→    all_gen_smiles = all_gen_smiles[:num_samples]
   245→    all_gen_smiles_digress = all_gen_smiles_digress[:num_samples]
   246→
   247→    valid_smiles = [s for s in all_gen_smiles if s]

   249→
   250→    validity = len(valid_smiles) / len(all_gen_smiles) if all_gen_smiles else 0
   251→    validity_digress = (
   252→        len(valid_smiles_digress) / len(all_gen_smiles_digress)
   253→        if all_gen_smiles_digress
   254→        else 0
   255→    )
   256→
   257→    return validity, validity_digress, valid_smiles

   109→
   110→def _get_available_port() -> int:
   111→    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
   112→        # A "" host address means INADDR_ANY i.e. binding to all interfaces.
   113→        # Note this is not compatible with IPv6.
   114→        s.bind(("", 0))
   115→        port = s.getsockname()[1]
   116→        return port
   117→
   118→
   119→_TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_ENV_VARS = (
   120→    "MASTER_ADDR",
   121→    "MASTER_PORT",
   122→    "RANK",
   123→    "WORLD_SIZE",
   124→    "LOCAL_RANK",
   125→    "LOCAL_WORLD_SIZE",
   126→)
   127→
   128→
   129→def _collect_env_vars() -> Dict[str, str]:
   130→    return {
   131→        env_var: os.environ[env_var]
   132→        for env_var in _TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_ENV_VARS
   133→        if env_var in os.environ
   134→    }
   135→
   136→
   137→def _is_slurm_job_process() -> bool:
   138→    return "SLURM_JOB_ID" in os.environ
   139→
   140→
   141→def _parse_slurm_node_list(s: str) -> List[str]:
   142→    nodes = []
   143→    # Extract "hostname", "hostname[1-2,3,4-5]," substrings
   144→    p = re.compile(r"(([^\[]+)(?:\[([^\]]+)\])?),?")
   145→    for m in p.finditer(s):
   146→        prefix, suffixes = s[m.start(2) : m.end(2)], s[m.start(3) : m.end(3)]
   147→        for suffix in suffixes.split(","):
   148→            span = suffix.split("-")
   149→            if len(span) == 1:
   150→                nodes.append(prefix + suffix)
   151→            else:
   152→                width = len(span[0])
   153→                start, end = int(span[0]), int(span[1]) + 1
   154→                nodes.extend([prefix + f"{i:0{width}}" for i in range(start, end)])
   155→    return nodes
   156→
   157→
   158→def _check_env_variable(key: str, new_value: str):
   159→    # Only check for difference with preset environment variables
   160→    if key in os.environ and os.environ[key] != new_value:
   161→        raise RuntimeError(
   162→            f"Cannot export environment variables as {key} is already set"
   163→        )
   164→
   165→
   166→class _TorchDistributedEnvironment:
   167→    def __init__(self):
   168→        self.master_addr = "127.0.0.1"
   169→        self.master_port = 0
   170→        self.rank = -1
   171→        self.world_size = -1
   172→        self.local_rank = -1
   173→        self.local_world_size = -1
   174→
   175→        env_vars = _collect_env_vars()
   176→        if len(env_vars) == len(_TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_ENV_VARS):
   177→            # Environment is fully set (e.g. by torchrun) — takes priority over Slurm
   178→            return self._set_from_preset_env()
   179→        elif _is_slurm_job_process():
   180→            return self._set_from_slurm_env()
   181→        elif not env_vars:
   182→            # Environment is not set
   183→            pass
   184→        else:
   185→            # Environment is partially set
   186→            collected_env_vars = ", ".join(env_vars.keys())
   187→            raise RuntimeError(f"Partially set environment: {collected_env_vars}")
   188→
   189→        if torch.cuda.device_count() > 0:
   190→            return self._set_from_local()
   191→
   192→        raise RuntimeError("Can't initialize PyTorch distributed environment")
   193→
   194→    # Slurm job created with sbatch, submitit, etc...
   195→    def _set_from_slurm_env(self):
   196→        # logger.info("Initialization from Slurm environment")
   197→        job_id = int(os.environ["SLURM_JOB_ID"])
   198→        node_count = int(os.environ["SLURM_JOB_NUM_NODES"])
   199→        nodes = _parse_slurm_node_list(os.environ["SLURM_JOB_NODELIST"])
   200→        assert len(nodes) == node_count
   201→
   202→        self.master_addr = nodes[0]
   203→        self.master_port = _get_master_port(seed=job_id)
   204→        self.rank = int(os.environ["SLURM_PROCID"])
   205→        self.world_size = int(os.environ["SLURM_NTASKS"])
   206→        assert self.rank < self.world_size
   207→        self.local_rank = int(os.environ["SLURM_LOCALID"])
   208→        self.local_world_size = self.world_size // node_count
   209→        assert self.local_rank < self.local_world_size
   210→
   211→    # Single node job with preset environment (i.e. torchrun)
   212→    def _set_from_preset_env(self):
   213→        # logger.info("Initialization from preset environment")
   214→        self.master_addr = os.environ["MASTER_ADDR"]
   215→        self.master_port = os.environ["MASTER_PORT"]
   216→        self.rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
   217→        self.world_size = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
   218→        assert self.rank < self.world_size
   219→        self.local_rank = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])
   220→        self.local_world_size = int(os.environ["LOCAL_WORLD_SIZE"])
   221→        assert self.local_rank < self.local_world_size
   222→
   223→    # Single node and GPU job (i.e. local script run)
   224→    def _set_from_local(self):
   225→        # logger.info("Initialization from local")
   226→        self.master_addr = "127.0.0.1"
   227→        self.master_port = _get_available_port()
   228→        self.rank = 0
   229→        self.world_size = 1
   230→        self.local_rank = 0
   231→        self.local_world_size = 1
   232→
   233→    def export(self, *, overwrite: bool) -> "_TorchDistributedEnvironment":
   234→        # See the "Environment variable initialization" section from
   235→        # https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.html for the complete list of
   236→        # environment variables required for the env:// initialization method.
   237→        env_vars = {
   238→            "MASTER_ADDR": self.master_addr,
   239→            "MASTER_PORT": str(self.master_port),
   240→            "RANK": str(self.rank),
   241→            "WORLD_SIZE": str(self.world_size),
   242→            "LOCAL_RANK": str(self.local_rank),
   243→            "LOCAL_WORLD_SIZE": str(self.local_world_size),
   244→        }
   245→        if not overwrite:
   246→            for k, v in env_vars.items():
   247→                _check_env_variable(k, v)
   248→
   249→        os.environ.update(env_vars)
   250→        return self
   251→
   252→
   253→def enable(
   254→    *,
   255→    set_cuda_current_device: bool = True,
   256→    overwrite: bool = False,
   257→    allow_nccl_timeout: bool = False,
   258→    main_rank: str = "first",
   259→):
   260→    """Enable distributed mode
   261→
   262→    Args:
   263→        set_cuda_current_device: If True, call torch.cuda.set_device() to set the
   264→            current PyTorch CUDA device to the one matching the local rank.
   265→        overwrite: If True, overwrites already set variables. Else fails.
   266→    """
   267→
   268→    global _LOCAL_RANK, _LOCAL_WORLD_SIZE
   269→    if _LOCAL_RANK >= 0 or _LOCAL_WORLD_SIZE >= 0:
   270→        raise RuntimeError("Distributed mode has already been enabled")
   271→    torch_env = _TorchDistributedEnvironment()
   272→    torch_env.export(overwrite=overwrite)
   273→
   274→    if set_cuda_current_device:
   275→        torch.cuda.set_device(torch_env.local_rank)
   276→
   277→    if allow_nccl_timeout:
   278→        # This allows to use torch distributed timeout in a NCCL backend
   279→        key, value = "NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING", "1"
   280→        if not overwrite:
   281→            _check_env_variable(key, value)
   282→        os.environ[key] = value
   283→
   284→    dist.init_process_group(
   285→        backend="nccl",
   286→        world_size=torch_env.world_size,
   287→        rank=torch_env.rank,
   288→        device_id=torch.device("cuda", torch_env.local_rank),
   289→    )
   290→    dist.barrier()
   291→
   292→    # Set the main rank to another one than 0 for printing processeces of other
   293→    # distributed setups.
   294→    if main_rank == "last":
   295→        main_rank = get_global_size() - 1
   296→
   297→    else:
   298→        main_rank = 0
   299→
   300→    set_main_rank(main_rank)
   301→
   302→    # Finalize setup
   303→    _LOCAL_RANK = torch_env.local_rank
   304→    _LOCAL_WORLD_SIZE = torch_env.local_world_size
   305→    _restrict_print_to_main_process()
   306→

1→import torch
     2→import torch.distributed as dist
     3→
     4→from torch.distributed.checkpoint import load, save
     5→from torch.distributed.checkpoint.state_dict import (
     6→    get_state_dict,
     7→    set_state_dict,
     8→    StateDictOptions,
     9→)
    10→from torch.distributed.pipelining import pipeline, SplitPoint
    11→
    12→from annotix_ml.distributed import get_global_rank, get_global_size
    13→
    14→
    15→def auto_model_split(model, example_input_args):
    16→    num_stages = get_global_size()
    17→    stage_id = get_global_rank()
    18→
    19→    num_layers = len(model.layers)
    20→
    21→    # Calculate split points to divide num_layers into num_stages blocks
    22→    split_indices = []
    23→    for i in range(1, num_stages):
    24→        idx = (i * num_layers) // num_stages
    25→        if 0 < idx < num_layers:
    26→            split_indices.append(idx)
    27→
    28→    split_dict = {f"layers.{idx}": SplitPoint.BEGINNING for idx in split_indices}
    29→
    30→    print("INIT : Distributed Pipeline Parallelism")
    31→    print(
    32→        *(
    33→            f"Shape of input {k}: {inp.shape}"
    34→            for k, inp in enumerate(example_input_args)
    35→        ),
    36→        sep="\n",
    37→    )
    38→
    39→    pipe = pipeline(
    40→        module=model,
    41→        mb_args=example_input_args,
    42→        split_spec=split_dict,
    43→    )
    44→
    45→    device = torch.device("cuda", stage_id)
    46→    train_stage = pipe.build_stage(stage_id, device=device)
    47→    eval_stage = pipe.build_stage(stage_id, device=device)
    48→    return train_stage, eval_stage
    49→
    50→
    51→def save_checkpoint(model, optimizer, path):
    52→    dist.barrier()
    53→    model_state, optimizer_state = get_state_dict(
    54→        model, optimizer, options=StateDictOptions(full_state_dict=True)
    55→    )
    56→    save(
    57→        {"model": model_state, "optimizer": optimizer_state},
    58→        checkpoint_id=path,  # each rank will save its own file
    59→    )
    60→    dist.barrier()
    61→
    62→
    63→def load_checkpoint(model, optimizer, path):
    64→    dist.barrier()
    65→    model_state, optimizer_state = get_state_dict(
    66→        model, optimizer, options=StateDictOptions(full_state_dict=True)
    67→    )
    68→    load(
    69→        {"model": model_state, "optimizer": optimizer_state},
    70→        checkpoint_id=path,  # each rank will save its own file
    71→    )
    72→    # necessary if model.load_state_dict() should be called
    73→    set_state_dict(
    74→        model,
    75→        optimizer,
    76→        model_state_dict=model_state,
    77→        optim_state_dict=optimizer_state,
    78→        options=StateDictOptions(broadcast_from_rank0=True, full_state_dict=True),
    79→    )
    80→    dist.barrier()

1→import torch
     2→import torch.nn as nn
     3→
     4→from annotix_ml.graphtransf.math.noising import (
     5→    cosine_beta_schedule_discrete,
     6→    sample_discrete_features,
     7→)
     8→
     9→
    10→class NoisingModel(nn.Module):
    11→    """
    12→    Torch module implementing the noise addition of the model.
    13→
    14→    Args:
    15→        nodes_distribution (torch.Tensor): The nodes distribution of the dataset used (natoms).
    16→        edges_distribution (torch.Tensor): The edges distribution of the dataset used (nbonds).
    17→        diffusion_steps (int): Number of diffusion steps possible.
    18→        noise_schedule_type (str, optional): The type of noise schedule to use. Defaults to "cosine".
    19→    """
    20→
    21→    def __init__(
    22→        self,
    23→        nodes_distribution: torch.Tensor,
    24→        edges_distribution: torch.Tensor,
    25→        diffusion_steps: int,
    26→        noise_schedule_type: str = "cosine",
    27→    ):
    28→        """
    29→        Initialize the NoisingModel.
    30→
    31→        Args:
    32→            nodes_distribution (torch.Tensor): The nodes distribution of the dataset used (natoms).
    33→            edges_distribution (torch.Tensor): The edges distribution of the dataset used (nbonds).
    34→            diffusion_steps (int): Number of diffusion steps possible.
    35→            noise_schedule_type (str, optional): The type of noise schedule to use. Defaults to "cosine".
    36→        """
    37→        super().__init__()
    38→        self.T = diffusion_steps
    39→        self.n_m = nodes_distribution
    40→        self.e_m = edges_distribution
    41→        self.natoms = len(nodes_distribution)
    42→        self.nbonds = len(edges_distribution)
    43→
    44→        match noise_schedule_type:
    45→            case "cosine":
    46→                alphas, alphas_bar = cosine_beta_schedule_discrete(diffusion_steps)
    47→
    48→            case _:
    49→                raise ValueError(f"{noise_schedule_type} not comprehensible.")
    50→
    51→        self.alphas = alphas
    52→        self.alphas_bar = alphas_bar
    53→
    54→    def get_Q_t(self, t: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    55→        """
    56→        Returns the nodes and edges matrices of diffusion from step t-1 to t.
    57→
    58→        Args:
    59→            t (int): The current time step.
    60→
    61→        Returns:
    62→            tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: The nodes and edges diffusion matrices.
    63→        """
    64→        alpha = self.alphas[int(t)]
    65→        device = self.alphas.device
    66→        Q_nodes = alpha * torch.eye(len(self.n_m), device=device) + (
    67→            1 - alpha
    68→        ) * self.n_m.unsqueeze(-1).expand(-1, self.natoms)  # (natoms, natoms)
    69→
    70→        Q_edges = alpha * torch.eye(len(self.e_m), device=device) + (
    71→            1 - alpha
    72→        ) * self.e_m.unsqueeze(-1).expand(-1, self.nbonds)  # (nbonds, nbonds)
    73→
    74→        return Q_nodes.T, Q_edges.T
    75→
    76→    def get_Q_bar_t(self, t: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    77→        """
    78→        Returns the nodes and edges matrices of diffusion from step 0 to t.
    79→
    80→        Args:
    81→            t (int): The current time step.
    82→
    83→        Returns:
    84→            tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: The nodes and edges diffusion matrices from 0 to t.
    85→        """
    86→        alpha_bar = self.alphas_bar[int(t)]
    87→        device = self.alphas_bar.device
    88→        Q_bar_nodes = alpha_bar * torch.eye(len(self.n_m), device=device) + (
    89→            1 - alpha_bar
    90→        ) * self.n_m.unsqueeze(-1).expand(-1, self.natoms)  # (natoms, natoms)
    91→
    92→        Q_bar_edges = alpha_bar * torch.eye(len(self.e_m), device=device) + (
    93→            1 - alpha_bar
    94→        ) * self.e_m.unsqueeze(-1).expand(-1, self.nbonds)  # (nbonds, nbonds)
    95→
    96→        return Q_bar_nodes.T, Q_bar_edges.T
    97→
    98→    def get_posterior(
    99→        self, N: torch.Tensor, E: torch.Tensor, t: int, eps: float = 1e-6
   100→    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
   101→        """
   102→        Compute the posterior distribution of nodes and edges at step t-1 given step t.
   103→
   104→        According to the formula of Vignac it is :
   105→        Z^t @ (Q^t)' * Z^0 @ Q_bar^(t-1) / Z^0 @ Q_bar^t @ (Z^t)'
   106→
   107→        Args:
   108→            N (torch.Tensor): The nodes one-hot encoded vector at step t.
   109→            E (torch.Tensor): The edges one-hot encoded vector at step t.
   110→            t (int): The current time step.
   111→            eps (float, optional): The value to add to the sum and avoid zero div. Defaults to 1e-6.
   112→
   113→        Returns:
   114→            tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: The posterior probabilities for nodes and edges at step t-1.
   115→                The proba are computed for each possible values of N^0 and E^0 making them resp
   116→                (bs, n, natoms, natoms) and (bs, n, n, nbonds, nbonds) tensors.
   117→        """
   118→        Q_n, Q_e = self.get_Q_t(t)  #  (natoms, natoms), (nbonds, nbonds)
   119→        Q_bar_n, Q_bar_e = self.get_Q_bar_t(t)  #  (natoms, natoms), (nbonds, nbonds)
   120→        Q_bar_nb, Q_bar_eb = self.get_Q_bar_t(
   121→            t - 1
   122→        )  #  (natoms, natoms), (nbonds, nbonds)
   123→
   124→        # Compute the posterior distribution of Nodes
   125→        # Start with the numerator of the equation
   126→        # N @ Q_n.T: (bs, n, natoms)
   127→        pN_numerator = (N @ Q_n.T).unsqueeze(2)  # (bs, n, 1, natoms)
   128→        pN_numerator = pN_numerator * Q_bar_nb.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(
   129→            0
   130→        )  # (bs, n, natoms, natoms)
   131→
   132→        # Continue with the denominator
   133→        pN_denominator = (N @ Q_bar_n.T).unsqueeze(-1)  # (bs, n, natoms, 1)
   134→
   135→        # Compute the posterior
   136→        pN_posterior = pN_numerator / (pN_denominator + eps)
   137→
   138→        # Compute the posterior distribution of Edges
   139→        pE_numerator = (E @ Q_e.T).unsqueeze(3)  # (bs, n, n, 1, nbonds)
   140→        pE_numerator = pE_numerator * Q_bar_eb.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(
   141→            0
   142→        )  # (bs, n, n, nbonds, nbonds)
   143→
   144→        # Compute the denominator
   145→        pE_denominator = (E @ Q_bar_e.T).unsqueeze(-1)  # (bs, n, n, nbonds, 1)
   146→
   147→        # Compute the posterior
   148→        pE_posterior = pE_numerator / (pE_denominator + eps)
   149→
   150→        return (
   151→            pN_posterior,
   152→            pE_posterior,
   153→        )  # (bs, n, natoms, natoms) and (bs, n, n, nbonds, nbonds)
   154→
   155→    @torch.no_grad
   156→    def forward(
   157→        self,
   158→        N: torch.Tensor,
   159→        E: torch.Tensor,
   160→        node_mask: torch.Tensor,
   161→        t: torch.Tensor | None = None,
   162→    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
   163→        """
   164→        Noise the nodes and edges matrices of a given batch.
   165→
   166→        If t is not provided, a random t is sampled for each graph.
   167→        The edges and nodes are noised with the corresponding matrices.
   168→
   169→        Args:
   170→            N (torch.Tensor): The nodes one-hot encoded vector.
   171→            E (torch.Tensor): The edges one-hot encoded vector.
   172→            node_mask (torch.Tensor): The mask vector.
   173→            t (torch.Tensor, optional): The time step(s) to noise to. Defaults to None.
   174→
   175→        Returns:
   176→            tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: A tuple containing:
   177→                - noised_N (torch.Tensor): Noised nodes features.
   178→                - noised_E (torch.Tensor): Noised edges features.
   179→                - sampled_t (torch.Tensor): The time steps used for noising.
   180→        """
   181→        # N (bs, n, natoms)
   182→        # E (bs, n, n, nbonds)
   183→
   184→        bs = N.shape[0]
   185→        device = N.device
   186→        if t is None:
   187→            sampled_t = torch.randint(1, self.T, (bs,), device=device)
   188→        else:
   189→            sampled_t = t.to(device)
   190→            if sampled_t.dim() == 2:
   191→                sampled_t = sampled_t.squeeze(1)
   192→
   193→        noised_N, noised_E = self.compute_noised_graph(N, E, sampled_t, node_mask)
   194→
   195→        return noised_N, noised_E, sampled_t.unsqueeze(1)
   196→
   197→    def compute_noised_graph(
   198→        self,
   199→        N: torch.Tensor,
   200→        E: torch.Tensor,
   201→        t: int | torch.Tensor,
   202→        node_mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,
   203→    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
   204→        """
   205→        Compute the noised graph at a given step t.
   206→
   207→        Args:
   208→            N (torch.Tensor): The nodes one-hot encoded vector.
   209→            E (torch.Tensor): The edges one-hot encoded vector.
   210→            t (int | torch.Tensor): The time step(s) to noise to.
   211→            node_mask (torch.Tensor, optional): The mask vector. Defaults to None.
   212→
   213→        Returns:
   214→            tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: The noised nodes and edges.
   215→        """
   216→        # Handle unbatched input
   217→        is_unbatched = N.dim() == 2
   218→        if is_unbatched:
   219→            N = N.unsqueeze(0)
   220→            E = E.unsqueeze(0)
   221→            if node_mask is None:
   222→                node_mask = torch.ones(N.shape[0], N.shape[1], device=N.device)
   223→            else:
   224→                node_mask = node_mask.unsqueeze(0)
   225→
   226→        if node_mask is None:
   227→            raise ValueError("node_mask must be provided.")
   228→
   229→        # Now N is (bs, n, natoms), E is (bs, n, n, nbonds)
   230→        bs = N.shape[0]
   231→        device = N.device
   232→        type_tensor = N.dtype
   233→
   234→        if isinstance(t, int):
   235→            t_tensor = torch.full((bs,), t, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
   236→        else:
   237→            t_tensor = t.to(device)
   238→            if t_tensor.dim() == 0:
   239→                t_tensor = t_tensor.unsqueeze(0)
   240→
   241→        # Make the matrices & stack them
   242→        Q_matrices = [self.get_Q_bar_t(int(t_val.item())) for t_val in t_tensor]
   243→        Q_bar_nodes, Q_bar_edges = zip(
   244→            *Q_matrices
   245→        )  # (natoms, natoms), (nbonds, nbonds)
   246→
   247→        Q_nodes = torch.stack(Q_bar_nodes).to(device)  # (bs, natoms, natoms)
   248→        Q_edges = (
   249→            torch.stack(Q_bar_edges).unsqueeze(1).to(device)
   250→        )  # (bs, 1, nbonds, nbonds)
   251→
   252→        # Do the noising
   253→        N = N @ Q_nodes  # (bs, n, natoms)
   254→        E = E @ Q_edges  # (bs, n, n, nbonds)
   255→
   256→        # Sample discrete features
   257→        N, E = sample_discrete_features(N, E, node_mask)
   258→
   259→        # Cast back to the original type
   260→        N = N.to(type_tensor)
   261→        E = E.to(type_tensor)
   262→
   263→        if is_unbatched:
   264→            return N.squeeze(0), E.squeeze(0)
   265→
   266→        return N, E
   267→
   268→    def move_to(self, device: torch.device) -> None:
   269→        """
   270→        Move the noiser to the specified device.
   271→
   272→        Args:
   273→            device (torch.device): The device to move the noiser to.
   274→        """
   275→        self.alphas = self.alphas.to(device)
   276→        self.alphas_bar = self.alphas_bar.to(device)
   277→        self.n_m = self.n_m.to(device)
   278→        self.e_m = self.e_m.to(device)

1→import torch
     2→import torch.nn as nn
     3→from annotix_ml.graphtransf.data.data_utils import mask_any_tensor
     4→
     5→
     6→def digress_loss(
     7→    pN: torch.Tensor,
     8→    pE: torch.Tensor,
     9→    N: torch.Tensor,
    10→    E: torch.Tensor,
    11→    mask: torch.Tensor,
    12→    loss_ratio: float,
    13→    return_all: bool = False,
    14→) -> torch.Tensor | tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    15→    """
    16→    Compute the loss based on prediction and target tensors.
    17→
    18→    Args:
    19→        pN (torch.Tensor): Predicted node probabilities of shape (bs, n, natoms).
    20→        pE (torch.Tensor): Predicted edge probabilities of shape (bs, n, n, nedges).
    21→        N (torch.Tensor): Target node features of shape (bs, n, natoms).
    22→        E (torch.Tensor): Target edge features of shape (bs, n, n, nedges).
    23→        mask (torch.Tensor): Mask tensor of shape (bs, n).
    24→        loss_ratio (float): Weight of the edge loss in the total loss.
    25→        return_all (bool, optional): If True, returns (total_loss, Nloss, Eloss). Defaults to False.
    26→
    27→    Returns:
    28→        torch.Tensor | tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    29→            Scalar total loss value or tuple of losses.
    30→    """
    31→    ce_loss = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    32→
    33→    # Node loss
    34→    N_target = N.argmax(-1)  # (bs, n)
    35→    N_target = mask_any_tensor(
    36→        N_target, mask, fill=-100
    37→    )  # -100 is the ignore_index of CrossEntropLoss
    38→    pN = pN.transpose(1, 2)  # (bs, n_atoms, n)
    39→
    40→    Nloss = ce_loss(pN, N_target)
    41→
    42→    # Edges loss
    43→    E_target = E.argmax(-1)  # (bs, n, n)
    44→    E_target = mask_any_tensor(
    45→        E_target, mask, fill=-100
    46→    )  # -100 is the ignore_index of CrossEntropLoss
    47→    pE = pE.permute((0, 3, 1, 2))  # (bs, n_edges, n, n)
    48→
    49→    Eloss = ce_loss(pE, E_target)
    50→
    51→    # Add the losses
    52→    total_loss = Nloss + (loss_ratio * Eloss)
    53→
    54→    if return_all:
    55→        return total_loss, Nloss, Eloss
    56→
    57→    return total_loss
    58→
